1.17.s:
sūta uvāca
evaṃ saṃkṣepataḥ proktaḥ sahyādīnāṃ samudbhavaḥ
yaḥ paṭhecchṛṇuyādvāpi śrāvayedvā dvijottamān //
1.17.d:
सूत उवाच
एवं संक्षेपतः प्रोक्तः सह्यादीनां समुद्भवः
यः पठेच्छृणुयाद्वापि श्रावयेद्वा द्विजोत्तमान् ॥
1.17.m: Sūta said: / Thus has been declared in brief the origin of the [Kumāras] beginning with Sahya. / Whoever reads this, hears it, or recites it to the foremost of the twice-born

1.17.s:
sa yāti brahmasāyujyaṃ prasādātparameṣṭhinaḥ
kathaṃ liṅgamabhūlliṅge samabhyarcyaḥ sa śaṅkaraḥ //
1.17.d:
स याति ब्रह्मसायुज्यं प्रसादात्परमेष्ठिनः
कथं लिङ्गमभूल्लिङ्गे समभ्यर्च्यः स शङ्करः ॥
1.17.m: attains union with Brahman through the grace of the Supreme Being. / How did the liṅga come to be? In what manner is Śaṅkara to be worshipped in the liṅga?

1.17.s:
kiṃ liṅgaṃ kas tathā liṅgī sūta vaktumihārhasi
evaṃ devāś ca ṛṣayaḥ praṇipatya pitāmaham //
1.17.d:
किं लिङ्गं कस् तथा लिङ्गी सूत वक्तुमिहार्हसि
एवं देवाश् च ऋषयः प्रणिपत्य पितामहम् ॥
1.17.m: What is the liṅga, and who is the possessor of the liṅga? O Sūta, you ought to tell this here. / Thus the gods and the sages, having bowed down before Pitāmaha,

1.17.s:
apṛcchan bhagavaṃlliṅgaṃ kathamāsīditi svayam
liṅge maheśvaro rudraḥ samabhyarcyaḥ kathaṃ tviti //
1.17.d:
अपृच्छन् भगवंल्लिङ्गं कथमासीदिति स्वयम्
लिङ्गे महेश्वरो रुद्रः समभ्यर्च्यः कथं त्विति ॥
1.17.m: asked: 'O blessed one, how did the liṅga come to be of itself? / And how is Maheśvara Rudra to be worshipped in the liṅga?

1.17.s:
kiṃ liṅgaṃ kas tathā liṅgī so 'pyāha ca pitāmahaḥ
pradhānaṃ liṅgamākhyātaṃ liṅgī ca parameśvaraḥ //
1.17.d:
किं लिङ्गं कस् तथा लिङ्गी सो ऽप्याह च पितामहः
प्रधानं लिङ्गमाख्यातं लिङ्गी च परमेश्वरः ॥
1.17.m: What is the liṅga, and who is the possessor of the liṅga?' And Pitāmaha spoke: / 'Pradhāna is said to be the liṅga, and the Supreme Lord is the possessor of the liṅga.

1.17.s:
rakṣārthamaṃbudhau mahyaṃ viṣṇostvāsīt surottamāḥ
vaimānike gate sarge janalokaṃ saharṣibhiḥ //
1.17.d:
रक्षार्थमंबुधौ मह्यं विष्णोस्त्वासीत् सुरोत्तमाः
वैमानिके गते सर्गे जनलोकं सहर्षिभिः ॥
1.17.m: For protection in the cosmic ocean, O foremost of gods, there took place [an encounter] between Viṣṇu and me, / when the celestial creation had departed to Janaloka together with the sages.

1.17.s:
sthitikāle tadā pūrṇe tataḥ pratyāhṛte tathā
caturyugasahasrānte satyalokaṃ gate surāḥ //
1.17.d:
स्थितिकाले तदा पूर्णे ततः प्रत्याहृते तथा
चतुर्युगसहस्रान्ते सत्यलोकं गते सुराः ॥
1.17.m: When the period of maintenance was completed and thus [all] was withdrawn, / at the end of a thousand four-yuga cycles, when [the dwellers] had gone to Satyaloka, O gods,

1.17.s:
vinādhipatyaṃ samatāṃ gate 'nte brahmaṇo mama
śuṣke ca sthāvare sarve tv anāvṛṣṭyā ca sarvaśaḥ //
1.17.d:
विनाधिपत्यं समतां गते ऽन्ते ब्रह्मणो मम
शुष्के च स्थावरे सर्वे त्व् अनावृष्ट्या च सर्वशः ॥
1.17.m: and at the end [of the day] of mine, Brahmā, having reached an equality devoid of dominion, / all stationary things having dried up completely due to drought,

1.17.s:
paśavo mānuṣā vṛkṣāḥ piśācāḥ piśitāśanāḥ
gandharvādyāḥ krameṇaiva nirdagdhā bhānubhānubhiḥ //
1.17.d:
पशवो मानुषा वृक्षाः पिशाचाः पिशिताशनाः
गन्धर्वाद्याः क्रमेणैव निर्दग्धा भानुभानुभिः ॥
1.17.m: beasts, humans, trees, piśācas, flesh-eaters, / and Gandharvas and others were successively incinerated by the rays of the sun.

1.17.s:
ekārṇave mahāghore tamobhūte samantataḥ
suṣvāpāṃbhasi yogātmā nirmalo nirupaplavaḥ //
1.17.d:
एकार्णवे महाघोरे तमोभूते समन्ततः
सुष्वापांभसि योगात्मा निर्मलो निरुपप्लवः ॥
1.17.m: In the exceedingly terrible single ocean enveloped completely in darkness, / he whose nature is yoga, spotless and unassailed, slept upon the waters:

1.17.s:
sahasraśīrṣā viśvātmā sahasrākṣaḥ sahasrapāt
sahasrabāhuḥ sarvajñaḥ sarvadevabhavodbhavaḥ //
1.17.d:
सहस्रशीर्षा विश्वात्मा सहस्राक्षः सहस्रपात्
सहस्रबाहुः सर्वज्ञः सर्वदेवभवोद्भवः ॥
1.17.m: thousand-headed, the soul of the universe, thousand-eyed, thousand-footed, / thousand-armed, all-knowing, the source of the origin of all gods,

1.17.s:
hiraṇyagarbho rajasā tamasā śaṅkaraḥ svayam
sattvena sarvago viṣṇuḥ sarvātmatve maheśvaraḥ //
1.17.d:
हिरण्यगर्भो रजसा तमसा शङ्करः स्वयम्
सत्त्वेन सर्वगो विष्णुः सर्वात्मत्वे महेश्वरः ॥
1.17.m: Hiraṇyagarbha through rajas, Śaṅkara himself through tamas, / all-pervading Viṣṇu through sattva, and Maheśvara in being the Self of all,

1.17.s:
kālātmā kālanābhastu śuklaḥ kṛṣṇastu nirguṇaḥ
nārāyaṇo mahābāhuḥ sarvātmā sadasanmayaḥ //
1.17.d:
कालात्मा कालनाभस्तु शुक्लः कृष्णस्तु निर्गुणः
नारायणो महाबाहुः सर्वात्मा सदसन्मयः ॥
1.17.m: the embodiment of Time, whose navel is Time, white, black, attributeless, / Nārāyaṇa, the mighty-armed, the universal Self, consisting of both existence and non-existence.

1.17.s:
tathābhūtamahaṃ dṛṣṭvā śayānaṃ paṅkajekṣaṇam
māyayā mohitastasya tamavocamamarṣitaḥ //
1.17.d:
तथाभूतमहं दृष्ट्वा शयानं पङ्कजेक्षणम्
मायया मोहितस्तस्य तमवोचममर्षितः ॥
1.17.m: Seeing the lotus-eyed one lying thus, / bewildered by his māyā, I, indignant, said to him:

1.17.s:
kastvaṃ vadeti hastena samutthāpya sanātanam
tadā hastaprahāreṇa tīvreṇa sa dṛḍhena tu //
1.17.d:
कस्त्वं वदेति हस्तेन समुत्थाप्य सनातनम्
तदा हस्तप्रहारेण तीव्रेण स दृढेन तु ॥
1.17.m: "Tell me, who are you?", rousing the eternal one with my hand. / Then, struck by that sharp and forceful blow of the hand,

1.17.s:
prabuddho 'hīyaśayanāt samāsīnaḥ kṣaṇaṃ vaśī
dadarśa nidrāviklinnanīrajāmalalocanaḥ //
1.17.d:
प्रबुद्धो ऽहीयशयनात् समासीनः क्षणं वशी
ददर्श निद्राविक्लिन्ननीरजामललोचनः ॥
1.17.m: awakened from his serpent-bed, sitting up for a moment, the master of his senses, / his spotless lotus-eyes moist with sleep, gazed upon me.

1.17.s:
māmagre saṃsthitaṃ bhāsādhyāsito bhagavān hariḥ
āha cotthāya bhagavān hasanmāṃ madhuraṃ sakṛt //
1.17.d:
मामग्रे संस्थितं भासाध्यासितो भगवान् हरिः
आह चोत्थाय भगवान् हसन्मां मधुरं सकृत् ॥
1.17.m: Occupying [the space] with his splendor, the blessed Lord Hari, standing before me, / rose up and said, smiling sweetly at me once:

1.17.s:
svāgataṃsvāgataṃ vatsa pitāmaha mahādyute
tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā smitapūrvaṃ surarṣabhāḥ //
1.17.d:
स्वागतंस्वागतं वत्स पितामह महाद्युते
तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा स्मितपूर्वं सुरर्षभाः ॥
1.17.m: "Welcome, welcome, child, O Pitāmaha of great splendor!" / Hearing those words of his accompanied by a smile, O best of the gods,

1.17.s:
rajasā baddhavairaś ca tamavocaṃ janārdanam
bhāṣase vatsa vatseti sargasaṃhārakāraṇam //
1.17.d:
रजसा बद्धवैरश् च तमवोचं जनार्दनम्
भाषसे वत्स वत्सेति सर्गसंहारकारणम् ॥
1.17.m: my hostility aroused by rajas, I said to Janārdana: / "Do you speak to me, saying 'Child, child', to me the cause of creation and dissolution,

1.17.s:
mām ihāntaḥsmitaṃ kṛtvā guruḥ śiṣyamivānagha
kartāraṃ jagatāṃ sākṣāt prakṛteś ca pravartakam //
1.17.d:
माम् इहान्तःस्मितं कृत्वा गुरुः शिष्यमिवानघ
कर्तारं जगतां साक्षात् प्रकृतेश् च प्रवर्तकम् ॥
1.17.m: smiling inwardly here, O sinless one, as a teacher does to a disciple— / to me, the direct creator of the worlds and the impeller of Prakṛti,

1.17.s:
sanātanamajaṃ viṣṇuṃ viriñciṃ viśvasaṃbhavam
viśvātmānaṃ vidhātāraṃ dhātāraṃ paṅkajekṣaṇam //
1.17.d:
सनातनमजं विष्णुं विरिञ्चिं विश्वसंभवम्
विश्वात्मानं विधातारं धातारं पङ्कजेक्षणम् ॥
1.17.m: the eternal, the unborn, Viṣṇu, Viriñci, the source of the universe, / the soul of the universe, the ordainer, the creator, the lotus-eyed one?

1.17.s:
kimarthaṃ bhāṣase mohād vaktumarhasi satvaram
so 'pi māmāha jagatāṃ kartāhamiti lokaya //
1.17.d:
किमर्थं भाषसे मोहाद् वक्तुमर्हसि सत्वरम्
सो ऽपि मामाह जगतां कर्ताहमिति लोकय ॥
1.17.m: Why do you speak out of delusion? You must answer quickly!" / He too said to me: "Look! I am the creator of the worlds,

1.17.s:
bhartā hartā bhavān aṅgād avatīrṇo mamāvyayāt
vismṛto 'si jagannāthaṃ nārāyaṇamanāmayam //
1.17.d:
भर्ता हर्ता भवान् अङ्गाद् अवतीर्णो ममाव्ययात्
विस्मृतो ऽसि जगन्नाथं नारायणमनामयम् ॥
1.17.m: the sustainer, the destroyer. You have descended from my imperishable limb; / have you forgotten Nārāyaṇa, the free from affliction, the lord of the world,

1.17.s:
puruṣaṃ paramātmānaṃ puruhūtaṃ puruṣṭutam
viṣṇumacyutamīśānaṃ viśvasya prabhavodbhavam //
1.17.d:
पुरुषं परमात्मानं पुरुहूतं पुरुष्टुतम्
विष्णुमच्युतमीशानं विश्वस्य प्रभवोद्भवम् ॥
1.17.m: Puruṣa, the Supreme Self, invoked by many, praised by many, / Viṣṇu, Acyuta, Īśāna, the source of the origin of the universe?

1.17.s:
tavāparādho nāstyatra mama māyākṛtaṃ tvidam
śṛṇu satyaṃ caturvaktra sarvadeveśvaro hyayam //
1.17.d:
तवापराधो नास्त्यत्र मम मायाकृतं त्विदम्
शृणु सत्यं चतुर्वक्त्र सर्वदेवेश्वरो ह्ययम् ॥
1.17.m: There is no fault of yours in this; this is caused by my māyā. / Hear the truth, O four-faced one: this one is indeed the lord of all the gods,

1.17.s:
kartā netā ca hartā ca na mayāsti samo vibhuḥ
ahameva paraṃ brahma paraṃ tattvaṃ pitāmaha //
1.17.d:
कर्ता नेता च हर्ता च न मयास्ति समो विभुः
अहमेव परं ब्रह्म परं तत्त्वं पितामह ॥
1.17.m: the maker, the leader, and the destroyer; there is no all-pervading one equal to me. / I alone am the supreme Brahman, the supreme principle, O Pitāmaha.

1.17.s:
ahameva paraṃ jyotiḥ paramātmā tvahaṃ vibhuḥ
yadyaddṛṣṭaṃ śrutaṃ sarvaṃ jagatyasmiṃścarācaram //
1.17.d:
अहमेव परं ज्योतिः परमात्मा त्वहं विभुः
यद्यद्दृष्टं श्रुतं सर्वं जगत्यस्मिंश्चराचरम् ॥
1.17.m: I alone am the supreme light; I am the Supreme Self, the all-pervasive. / Whatever is seen or heard, all moving and unmoving things in this universe—

1.17.s:
tattadviddhi caturvaktra sarvaṃ manmayamityatha
mayā sṛṣṭaṃ purāvyaktaṃ caturviṃśatikaṃ svayam //
1.17.d:
तत्तद्विद्धि चतुर्वक्त्र सर्वं मन्मयमित्यथ
मया सृष्टं पुराव्यक्तं चतुर्विंशतिकं स्वयम् ॥
1.17.m: know each and every one of them, O four-faced one, to be made of me. / Formerly, the unmanifest composed of twenty-four principles was created by me myself.

1.17.s:
nityāntā hyaṇavo baddhāḥ sṛṣṭāḥ krodhodbhavādayaḥ
prasādāddhi bhavānaṇḍāny anekānīha līlayā //
1.17.d:
नित्यान्ता ह्यणवो बद्धाः सृष्टाः क्रोधोद्भवादयः
प्रसादाद्धि भवानण्डान्य् अनेकानीह लीलया ॥
1.17.m: The bound atoms with eternal ends, and those born of anger and the rest were created. / Indeed, by my grace you [create] manifold cosmic eggs here in divine play.

1.17.s:
sṛṣṭā buddhirmayā tasyām ahaṅkārastridhā tataḥ
tanmātrāpañcakaṃ tasmān manaḥ ṣaṣṭhendriyāṇi ca //
1.17.d:
सृष्टा बुद्धिर्मया तस्याम् अहङ्कारस्त्रिधा ततः
तन्मात्रापञ्चकं तस्मान् मनः षष्ठेन्द्रियाणि च ॥
1.17.m: Intellect was created by me; within it arose egoity of threefold nature; / from that the five subtle elements, and from that the mind and the six senses,

1.17.s:
ākāśādīni bhūtāni bhautikāni ca līlayā
ityuktavati tasmiṃś ca mayi cāpi vacas tathā //
1.17.d:
आकाशादीनि भूतानि भौतिकानि च लीलया
इत्युक्तवति तस्मिंश् च मयि चापि वचस् तथा ॥
1.17.m: the gross elements beginning with space, and their products, in divine play." / While he spoke thus, and while I too spoke such words,

1.17.s:
āvayoścābhavadyuddhaṃ sughoraṃ romaharṣaṇam
pralayārṇavamadhye tu rajasā baddhavairayoḥ //
1.17.d:
आवयोश्चाभवद्युद्धं सुघोरं रोमहर्षणम्
प्रलयार्णवमध्ये तु रजसा बद्धवैरयोः ॥
1.17.m: there arose between us an exceedingly terrible battle making the hair stand on end, / in the midst of the ocean of cosmic dissolution, our enmity bound by rajas.

1.17.s:
etasminnantare liṅgam abhavaccāvayoḥ puraḥ
vivādaśamanārthaṃ hi prabodhārthaṃ ca bhāsvaram //
1.17.d:
एतस्मिन्नन्तरे लिङ्गम् अभवच्चावयोः पुरः
विवादशमनार्थं हि प्रबोधार्थं च भास्वरम् ॥
1.17.m: In the meantime, there appeared a liṅga before the two of us, / blazing, for the quelling of our dispute and for our awakening,

1.17.s:
jvālāmālāsahasrāḍhyaṃ kālānalaśatopamam
kṣayavṛddhivinirmuktam ādimadhyāntavarjitam //
1.17.d:
ज्वालामालासहस्राढ्यं कालानलशतोपमम्
क्षयवृद्धिविनिर्मुक्तम् आदिमध्यान्तवर्जितम् ॥
1.17.m: endowed with thousands of garlands of flames, resembling a hundred fires of dissolution, / free from decay and increase, devoid of beginning, middle, and end,

1.17.s:
anaupamyamanirdeśyam avyaktaṃ viśvasaṃbhavam
tasya jvālāsahasreṇa mohito bhagavān hariḥ //
1.17.d:
अनौपम्यमनिर्देश्यम् अव्यक्तं विश्वसंभवम्
तस्य ज्वालासहस्रेण मोहितो भगवान् हरिः ॥
1.17.m: incomparable, indefinable, unmanifest, the source of the universe. / Bewildered by its thousands of flames, the blessed Lord Hari,

1.17.s:
mohitaṃ prāha māmatra parīkṣāvo 'gnisaṃbhavam
adhogamiṣyāmyanalastaṃbhasyānupamasya ca //
1.17.d:
मोहितं प्राह मामत्र परीक्षावो ऽग्निसंभवम्
अधोगमिष्याम्यनलस्तंभस्यानुपमस्य च ॥
1.17.m: spoke to me, who was also bewildered: "Let the two of us examine this origin of fire; / I shall go downwards along this peerless pillar of fire,

1.17.s:
bhavānūrdhvaṃ prayatnena gantumarhasi satvaram
evaṃ vyāhṛtya viśvātmā svarūpamakarottadā //
1.17.d:
भवानूर्ध्वं प्रयत्नेन गन्तुमर्हसि सत्वरम्
एवं व्याहृत्य विश्वात्मा स्वरूपमकरोत्तदा ॥
1.17.m: and you should quickly go upwards with effort." / Having spoken thus, the soul of the universe then assumed a form.'

1.17.s:
vārāhamahamapyāśu haṃsatvaṃ prāptavānsurāḥ
tadāprabhṛti māmāhurh aṃsaṃ haṃso virāḍiti //
1.17.d:
वाराहमहमप्याशु हंसत्वं प्राप्तवान्सुराः
तदाप्रभृति मामाहुर्ह् अंसं हंसो विराडिति ॥
1.17.m: [Viṣṇu assumed] the form of a boar, and I quickly attained the state of a swan, O gods. / From then on, they have called me the Swan, the Swan who is Virāj.

1.17.s:
haṃsahaṃseti yo brūyān māṃ haṃsaḥ sa bhaviṣyati
suśveto hyanalākṣaś ca viśvataḥ pakṣasaṃyutaḥ //
1.17.d:
हंसहंसेति यो ब्रूयान् मां हंसः स भविष्यति
सुश्वेतो ह्यनलाक्षश् च विश्वतः पक्षसंयुतः ॥
1.17.m: Whoever says, 'Haṃsa, Haṃsa', shall become that swan, / radiant white, with fiery eyes, and endowed with wings on all sides.

1.17.s:
mano 'nilajavo bhūtvā gato 'haṃ cordhvataḥ surāḥ
nārāyaṇo 'pi viśvātmā nīlāñjanacayopamam //
1.17.d:
मनो ऽनिलजवो भूत्वा गतो ऽहं चोर्ध्वतः सुराः
नारायणो ऽपि विश्वात्मा नीलाञ्जनचयोपमम् ॥
1.17.m: Having attained the speed of mind and wind, I went upward, O gods. / Nārāyaṇa too, the Self of all, [assuming a form] resembling a heap of blue collyrium,

1.17.s:
daśayojanavistīrṇaṃ śatayojanamāyatam
meruparvatavarṣmāṇaṃ gauratīkṣṇāgradaṃṣṭriṇam //
1.17.d:
दशयोजनविस्तीर्णं शतयोजनमायतम्
मेरुपर्वतवर्ष्माणं गौरतीक्ष्णाग्रदंष्ट्रिणम् ॥
1.17.m: ten yojanas wide and a hundred yojanas long, / with the body [as vast as] Mount Meru, having white, sharp-tipped tusks,

1.17.s:
kālādityasamābhāsaṃ dīrghaghoṇaṃ mahāsvaram
hrasvapādaṃ vicitrāṅgaṃ jaitraṃ dṛḍham anaupamam //
1.17.d:
कालादित्यसमाभासं दीर्घघोणं महास्वरम्
ह्रस्वपादं विचित्राङ्गं जैत्रं दृढम् अनौपमम् ॥
1.17.m: blazing like the sun of dissolution, long-snouted, deep-voiced, / short-legged, variegated in limbs, victorious, firm, and matchless—

1.17.s:
vārāhamasitaṃ rūpam āsthāya gatavānadhaḥ
evaṃ varṣasahasraṃ tu tvaranviṣṇuradhogataḥ //
1.17.d:
वाराहमसितं रूपम् आस्थाय गतवानधः
एवं वर्षसहस्रं तु त्वरन्विष्णुरधोगतः ॥
1.17.m: assuming that black form of a boar, he went downward. / Thus for a thousand years Viṣṇu rushed downward,

1.17.s:
nāpaśyadalpamapyasya mūlaṃ liṅgasya sūkaraḥ
tāvatkālaṃ gato hyūrdhvam ahamapyarisūdanaḥ //
1.17.d:
नापश्यदल्पमप्यस्य मूलं लिङ्गस्य सूकरः
तावत्कालं गतो ह्यूर्ध्वम् अहमप्यरिसूदनः ॥
1.17.m: yet that boar could not see even the smallest bit of this liṅga's base. / For that same length of time, I too, the crusher of foes, flew upward,

1.17.s:
satvaraṃ sarvayatnena tasyāntaṃ jñātumicchayā
śrānto hyadṛṣṭvā tasyāntam ahaṅkārādadhogataḥ //
1.17.d:
सत्वरं सर्वयत्नेन तस्यान्तं ज्ञातुमिच्छया
श्रान्तो ह्यदृष्ट्वा तस्यान्तम् अहङ्कारादधोगतः ॥
1.17.m: hastening with all effort through a desire to know its end. / Weary indeed at not seeing its end, down I went out of [humbled] pride.

1.17.s:
tathaiva bhagavān viṣṇuḥ śrāntaḥ saṃtrastalocanaḥ
sarvadevabhavastūrṇam utthitaḥ saḥ mahāvapuḥ //
1.17.d:
तथैव भगवान् विष्णुः श्रान्तः संत्रस्तलोचनः
सर्वदेवभवस्तूर्णम् उत्थितः सः महावपुः ॥
1.17.m: Likewise, Lord Viṣṇu, weary, his eyes terrified, / he from whom all gods originate quickly rose up, of gigantic body.

1.17.s:
samāgato mayā sārdhaṃ praṇipatya mahāmanāḥ
māyayā mohitaḥ śaṃbhos tasthau saṃvignamānasaḥ //
1.17.d:
समागतो मया सार्धं प्रणिपत्य महामनाः
मायया मोहितः शंभोस् तस्थौ संविग्नमानसः ॥
1.17.m: Coming together with me, having bowed low, the noble-minded one, / deluded by the māyā of Śambhu, stood with an anxious mind.

1.17.s:
pṛṣṭhataḥ pārśvataścaiva cāgrataḥ parameśvaram
praṇipatya mayā sārdhaṃ sasmāra kimidaṃ tviti //
1.17.d:
पृष्ठतः पार्श्वतश्चैव चाग्रतः परमेश्वरम्
प्रणिपत्य मया सार्धं सस्मार किमिदं त्विति ॥
1.17.m: From behind, from the sides, and from the front, having prostrated / to the Supreme Lord together with me, he reflected: 'What can this be?'

1.17.s:
tadā samabhavattatra nādo vai śabdalakṣaṇaḥ
omomiti suraśreṣṭhāḥ suvyaktaḥ plutalakṣaṇaḥ //
1.17.d:
तदा समभवत्तत्र नादो वै शब्दलक्षणः
ओमोमिति सुरश्रेष्ठाः सुव्यक्तः प्लुतलक्षणः ॥
1.17.m: Then there arose a sound characterized by speech, / 'Oṃ, Oṃ', O best of gods, fully articulated with a prolated tone.

1.17.s:
kimidaṃ tviti saṃcintya mayā tiṣṭhanmahāsvanam
liṅgasya dakṣiṇe bhāge tadāpaśyatsanātanam //
1.17.d:
किमिदं त्विति संचिन्त्य मया तिष्ठन्महास्वनम्
लिङ्गस्य दक्षिणे भागे तदापश्यत्सनातनम् ॥
1.17.m: Thinking 'What is this?', standing with me, he then beheld that loud-sounding, / eternal [form] on the right side of the liṅga:

1.17.s:
ādyavarṇamakāraṃ tu ukāraṃ cottare tataḥ
makāraṃ madhyataścaiva nādāntaṃ tasya caumiti //
1.17.d:
आद्यवर्णमकारं तु उकारं चोत्तरे ततः
मकारं मध्यतश्चैव नादान्तं तस्य चौमिति ॥
1.17.m: the initial syllable 'A', then 'U' to the north, / 'M' in the middle, and 'Oṃ' as the end of its resonance.

1.17.s:
sūryamaṇḍalavaddṛṣṭvā varṇamādyaṃ tu dakṣiṇe
uttare pāvakaprakhyam ukāraṃ puruṣarṣabhaḥ //
1.17.d:
सूर्यमण्डलवद्दृष्ट्वा वर्णमाद्यं तु दक्षिणे
उत्तरे पावकप्रख्यम् उकारं पुरुषर्षभः ॥
1.17.m: Seeing the initial syllable to the right resembling the sun's orb, / and to the north the syllable 'U' resembling fire, that bull among men [Viṣṇu saw]

1.17.s:
śītāṃśumaṇḍalaprakhyaṃ makāraṃ madhyamaṃ tathā
tasyopari tadāpaśyac chuddhasphaṭikavat prabhum //
1.17.d:
शीतांशुमण्डलप्रख्यं मकारं मध्यमं तथा
तस्योपरि तदापश्यच् छुद्धस्फटिकवत् प्रभुम् ॥
1.17.m: the middle syllable 'M' resembling the moon's orb, / and above it he then beheld the Lord, like pure crystal,

1.17.s:
turīyātītam amṛtaṃ niṣkalaṃ nirupaplavam
nirdvandvaṃ kevalaṃ śūnyaṃ bāhyābhyantaravarjitam //
1.17.d:
तुरीयातीतम् अमृतं निष्कलं निरुपप्लवम्
निर्द्वन्द्वं केवलं शून्यं बाह्याभ्यन्तरवर्जितम् ॥
1.17.m: transcending the fourth [state], immortal, partless, untainted, / free of dualities, absolute, void, devoid of exterior and interior,

1.17.s:
sabāhyābhyantaraṃ caiva sabāhyābhyantarasthitam
ādimadhyāntarahitam ānandasyāpi kāraṇam //
1.17.d:
सबाह्याभ्यन्तरं चैव सबाह्याभ्यन्तरस्थितम्
आदिमध्यान्तरहितम् आनन्दस्यापि कारणम् ॥
1.17.m: yet having exterior and interior, abiding within both exterior and interior, / devoid of beginning, middle, and end, and the cause of bliss itself.

1.17.s:
mātrāstisrastvardhamātraṃ nādākhyaṃ brahmasaṃjñitam
ṛgyajuḥsāmavedā vai mātrārūpeṇa mādhavaḥ //
1.17.d:
मात्रास्तिस्रस्त्वर्धमात्रं नादाख्यं ब्रह्मसंज्ञितम्
ऋग्यजुःसामवेदा वै मात्रारूपेण माधवः ॥
1.17.m: The three morae, the half-mora called resonance (nāda), and named Brahman— / Mādhava [perceived] the Ṛg, Yajur, and Sāma Vedas in the form of these morae.

1.17.s:
vedaśabdebhya eveśaṃ viśvātmānamacintayat
tadābhavadṛṣirveda ṛṣeḥ sāratamaṃ śubham //
1.17.d:
वेदशब्देभ्य एवेशं विश्वात्मानमचिन्तयत्
तदाभवदृषिर्वेद ऋषेः सारतमं शुभम् ॥
1.17.m: From the Vedic sounds alone he meditated upon the Lord, the Self of all. / Then the Veda became a seer, the most auspicious essence of a seer.

1.17.s:
tenaiva ṛṣiṇā viṣṇur jñātavān parameśvaram
cintayā rahito rudro vāco yanmanasā saha //
1.17.d:
तेनैव ऋषिणा विष्णुर् ज्ञातवान् परमेश्वरम्
चिन्तया रहितो रुद्रो वाचो यन्मनसा सह ॥
1.17.m: By that very seer, Viṣṇu came to know the Supreme Lord, / Rudra who is beyond thought, from whom words, together with the mind,

1.17.s:
aprāpya taṃ nivartante vācyastvekākṣareṇa saḥ
ekākṣareṇa tadvācyam ṛtaṃ paramakāraṇam //
1.17.d:
अप्राप्य तं निवर्तन्ते वाच्यस्त्वेकाक्षरेण सः
एकाक्षरेण तद्वाच्यम् ऋतं परमकारणम् ॥
1.17.m: turn back without reaching him, yet who is expressed by the single syllable. / By the single syllable is he expressed—the Cosmic Order, the ultimate cause,

1.17.s:
satyamānandamamṛtaṃ paraṃ brahma parātparam
ekākṣarādakārākhyo bhagavānkanakāṇḍajaḥ //
1.17.d:
सत्यमानन्दममृतं परं ब्रह्म परात्परम्
एकाक्षरादकाराख्यो भगवान्कनकाण्डजः ॥
1.17.m: truth, bliss, the immortal, the supreme Brahman, higher than the highest. / From the single syllable, the Lord born of the golden egg is designated 'A';

1.17.s:
ekākṣarādukārākhyo hariḥ paramakāraṇam
ekākṣarānmakārākhyo bhagavānnīlalohitaḥ //
1.17.d:
एकाक्षरादुकाराख्यो हरिः परमकारणम्
एकाक्षरान्मकाराख्यो भगवान्नीललोहितः ॥
1.17.m: from the single syllable, Hari, the ultimate cause, is designated 'U'; / from the single syllable, the Lord Nīlalohita is designated 'M'.

1.17.s:
sargakartā tvakārākhyo hy ukārākhyastu mohakaḥ
makārākhyas tayor nityam anugrahakaro 'bhavat //
1.17.d:
सर्गकर्ता त्वकाराख्यो ह्य् उकाराख्यस्तु मोहकः
मकाराख्यस् तयोर् नित्यम् अनुग्रहकरो ऽभवत् ॥
1.17.m: The one called 'A' is the author of creation, while the one called 'U' is the deluder; / the one called 'M' perpetually bestows grace upon the two.

1.17.s:
makārākhyo vibhurbījī hy akāro bījamucyate
ukārākhyo hariryoniḥ pradhānapuruṣeśvaraḥ //
1.17.d:
मकाराख्यो विभुर्बीजी ह्य् अकारो बीजमुच्यते
उकाराख्यो हरिर्योनिः प्रधानपुरुषेश्वरः ॥
1.17.m: The all-pervading one called 'M' is the seed-bearer; 'A' is said to be the seed; / Hari called 'U' is the womb, the Lord of Pradhāna and Puruṣa.

1.17.s:
bījī ca bījaṃ tadyonir nādākhyaś ca maheśvaraḥ
bījī vibhajya cātmānaṃ svecchayā tu vyavasthitaḥ //
1.17.d:
बीजी च बीजं तद्योनिर् नादाख्यश् च महेश्वरः
बीजी विभज्य चात्मानं स्वेच्छया तु व्यवस्थितः ॥
1.17.m: The seed-bearer, the seed, and its womb—and Maheśvara is designated as the resonance (nāda). / The seed-bearer, having divided himself, abides by his own will.

1.17.s:
asya liṅgādabhūdbījam akāro bījinaḥ prabhoḥ
ukārayonau nikṣiptam avardhata samantataḥ //
1.17.d:
अस्य लिङ्गादभूद्बीजम् अकारो बीजिनः प्रभोः
उकारयोनौ निक्षिप्तम् अवर्धत समन्ततः ॥
1.17.m: From this liṅga of the seed-bearing Lord arose the seed, 'A'. / Cast into the womb of 'U', it grew on all sides.

1.17.s:
sauvarṇamabhavaccāṇḍam āveṣṭyādyaṃ tadakṣaram
anekābdaṃ tathā cāpsu divyamaṇḍaṃ vyavasthitam //
1.17.d:
सौवर्णमभवच्चाण्डम् आवेष्ट्याद्यं तदक्षरम्
अनेकाब्दं तथा चाप्सु दिव्यमण्डं व्यवस्थितम् ॥
1.17.m: A golden egg came into being, enclosing that first syllable, / and that divine egg remained in the waters for many years.

1.17.s:
tato varṣasahasrānte dvidhā kṛtamajodbhavam
aṇḍam apsu sthitaṃ sākṣād ādyākhyeneśvareṇa tu //
1.17.d:
ततो वर्षसहस्रान्ते द्विधा कृतमजोद्भवम्
अण्डम् अप्सु स्थितं साक्षाद् आद्याख्येनेश्वरेण तु ॥
1.17.m: Then, at the end of a thousand years, that egg born of the Unborn, / resting in the waters, was split in two by the Lord known as the Primal One.

1.17.s:
tasyāṇḍasya śubhaṃ haimaṃ kapālaṃ cordhvasaṃsthitam
jajñe yaddyaustadaparaṃ pṛthivī pañcalakṣaṇā //
1.17.d:
तस्याण्डस्य शुभं हैमं कपालं चोर्ध्वसंस्थितम्
जज्ञे यद्द्यौस्तदपरं पृथिवी पञ्चलक्षणा ॥
1.17.m: The auspicious golden upper half of that egg became the sky; / the other half became the earth, endowed with five characteristics.

1.17.s:
tasmādaṇḍodbhavo jajñe tv akārākhyaścaturmukhaḥ
sa sraṣṭā sarvalokānāṃ sa eva trividhaḥ prabhuḥ //
1.17.d:
तस्मादण्डोद्भवो जज्ञे त्व् अकाराख्यश्चतुर्मुखः
स स्रष्टा सर्वलोकानां स एव त्रिविधः प्रभुः ॥
1.17.m: From that egg was born the four-faced one called 'A'; / he is the creator of all the worlds, he alone is the threefold lord.

1.17.s:
evamomomiti proktam ityāhuryajuṣāṃ varāḥ
yajuṣāṃ vacanaṃ śrutvā ṛcaḥ sāmāni sādaram //
1.17.d:
एवमोमोमिति प्रोक्तम् इत्याहुर्यजुषां वराः
यजुषां वचनं श्रुत्वा ऋचः सामानि सादरम् ॥
1.17.m: Thus it is uttered, 'Oṃ, Oṃ'—so proclaimed the foremost of the Yajurvedins. / Hearing the words of the Yajus, the verses of the Ṛc and the Sāmans reverently [said],

1.17.s:
evameva hare brahmann ityāhuḥ śrutayastadā
tato vijñāya deveśaṃ yathāvacchrutisaṃbhavaiḥ //
1.17.d:
एवमेव हरे ब्रह्मन्न् इत्याहुः श्रुतयस्तदा
ततो विज्ञाय देवेशं यथावच्छ्रुतिसंभवैः ॥
1.17.m: 'It is truly so, O Hari! O Brahmā!'—so the Vedic scriptures said at that time. / Then, recognizing the Lord of gods properly through [verses] originating in the Veda,

1.17.s:
mantrairmaheśvaraṃ devaṃ tuṣṭāva sumahodayam
āvayoḥ stutisaṃtuṣṭo liṅge tasminnirañjanaḥ //
1.17.d:
मन्त्रैर्महेश्वरं देवं तुष्टाव सुमहोदयम्
आवयोः स्तुतिसंतुष्टो लिङ्गे तस्मिन्निरञ्जनः ॥
1.17.m: with mantras he praised the god Maheśvara, of exalted glory. / Pleased with the praise of us two, the untainted one within that liṅga,

1.17.s:
divyaṃ śabdamayaṃ rūpam āsthāya prahasan sthitaḥ
akārastasya mūrdhā tu lalāṭaṃ dīrghamucyate //
1.17.d:
दिव्यं शब्दमयं रूपम् आस्थाय प्रहसन् स्थितः
अकारस्तस्य मूर्धा तु ललाटं दीर्घमुच्यते ॥
1.17.m: assuming a divine form composed of sound, stood smiling. / The letter 'A' is his crown, and the long [‘Ā’] is called his forehead;

1.17.s:
ikāro dakṣiṇaṃ netram īkāro vāmalocanam
ukāro dakṣiṇaṃ śrotram ūkāro vāmamucyate //
1.17.d:
इकारो दक्षिणं नेत्रम् ईकारो वामलोचनम्
उकारो दक्षिणं श्रोत्रम् ऊकारो वाममुच्यते ॥
1.17.m: the letter 'I' is his right eye, the letter 'Ī' his left eye; / the letter 'U' is his right ear, and the letter 'Ū' is called his left;

1.17.s:
ṛkāro dakṣiṇaṃ tasya kapolaṃ parameṣṭhinaḥ
vāmaṃ kapolam ṝkāro ḷ ḹ nāsāpuṭe ubhe //
1.17.d:
ऋकारो दक्षिणं तस्य कपोलं परमेष्ठिनः
वामं कपोलम् ॠकारो ऌ ॡ नासापुटे उभे ॥
1.17.m: the letter 'Ṛ' is the right cheek of that Parameṣṭhin; / the letter 'Ṝ' is his left cheek, and 'Ḷ' and 'Ḹ' are his two nostrils;

1.17.s:
ekāram oṣṭhamūrddhvaś ca aikārastvadharo vibhoḥ
okāraś ca tathaukāro dantapaṅktidvayaṃ kramāt //
1.17.d:
एकारम् ओष्ठमूर्द्ध्वश् च ऐकारस्त्वधरो विभोः
ओकारश् च तथौकारो दन्तपङ्क्तिद्वयं क्रमात् ॥
1.17.m: the letter 'E' is the upper lip, and 'Ai' is the lower lip of the Lord; / 'O' and 'Au' are respectively his two rows of teeth;

1.17.s:
amastu tālunī tasya devadevasya dhīmataḥ
kādipañcākṣarāṇyasya pañca hastāni dakṣiṇe //
1.17.d:
अमस्तु तालुनी तस्य देवदेवस्य धीमतः
कादिपञ्चाक्षराण्यस्य पञ्च हस्तानि दक्षिणे ॥
1.17.m: the anusvāra 'Aṃ' is the palate of that wise God of gods. / The five letters beginning with 'ka' are his five right hands;

1.17.s:
cādipañcākṣarāṇyevaṃ pañca hastāni vāmataḥ
ṭādipañcākṣaraṃ pādas tādipañcākṣaraṃ tathā //
1.17.d:
चादिपञ्चाक्षराण्येवं पञ्च हस्तानि वामतः
टादिपञ्चाक्षरं पादस् तादिपञ्चाक्षरं तथा ॥
1.17.m: the five letters beginning with 'ca' likewise are his five left hands. / The five letters beginning with 'ṭa' are one foot, and the five letters beginning with 'ta' the other foot.

1.17.s:
pakāramudaraṃ tasya phakāraḥ pārśvamucyate
bakāro vāmapārśvaṃ vai bhakāraṃ skandhamasya tat //
1.17.d:
पकारमुदरं तस्य फकारः पार्श्वमुच्यते
बकारो वामपार्श्वं वै भकारं स्कन्धमस्य तत् ॥
1.17.m: The letter 'pa' is his belly; the letter 'pha' is called his flank; / the letter 'ba' is his left flank; the letter 'bha' is his shoulder;

1.17.s:
makāraṃ hṛdayaṃ śaṃbhor mahādevasya yoginaḥ
yakārādisakārāntaṃ vibhorvai sapta dhātavaḥ //
1.17.d:
मकारं हृदयं शंभोर् महादेवस्य योगिनः
यकारादिसकारान्तं विभोर्वै सप्त धातवः ॥
1.17.m: the letter 'ma' is the heart of Śambhu, the Mahādeva, the yogin. / The letters beginning with 'ya' and ending with 'sa' are the Lord's seven bodily elements;

1.17.s:
hakāra ātmarūpaṃ vai kṣakāraḥ krodha ucyate
taṃ dṛṣṭvā umayā sārdhaṃ bhagavantaṃ maheśvaram //
1.17.d:
हकार आत्मरूपं वै क्षकारः क्रोध उच्यते
तं दृष्ट्वा उमया सार्धं भगवन्तं महेश्वरम् ॥
1.17.m: the letter 'ha' is his self, and the letter 'kṣa' is called his wrath. / Seeing the Lord Maheśvara together with Umā,

1.17.s:
praṇamya bhagavān viṣṇuḥ punaścāpaśyadūrddhvataḥ
oṅkāraprabhavaṃ mantraṃ kalāpañcakasaṃyutam //
1.17.d:
प्रणम्य भगवान् विष्णुः पुनश्चापश्यदूर्द्ध्वतः
ओङ्कारप्रभवं मन्त्रं कलापञ्चकसंयुतम् ॥
1.17.m: and bowing low, the Lord Viṣṇu again looked upward / at the mantra originating from the Oṅkāra, endowed with the five kalās,

1.17.s:
śuddhasphaṭikasaṃkāśaṃ subhāṣṭatriṃśadakṣaram
medhākaram abhūdbhūyaḥ sarvadharmārthasādhakam //
1.17.d:
शुद्धस्फटिकसंकाशं सुभाष्टत्रिंशदक्षरम्
मेधाकरम् अभूद्भूयः सर्वधर्मार्थसाधकम् ॥
1.17.m: resembling pure crystal, having thirty-eight auspicious syllables, / producing intellect, achieving all dharma and wealth.

1.17.s:
gāyatrīprabhavaṃ mantraṃ haritaṃ vaśyakārakam
caturviṃśativarṇāḍhyaṃ catuṣkalamanuttamam //
1.17.d:
गायत्रीप्रभवं मन्त्रं हरितं वश्यकारकम्
चतुर्विंशतिवर्णाढ्यं चतुष्कलमनुत्तमम् ॥
1.17.m: [He saw] the green mantra originating from the Gāyatrī, causing subjugation, / rich in twenty-four syllables, having four kalās, unsurpassed;

1.17.s:
atharvamasitaṃ mantraṃ kalāṣṭakasamāyutam
abhicārikamatyarthaṃ trayastriṃśacchubhākṣaram //
1.17.d:
अथर्वमसितं मन्त्रं कलाष्टकसमायुतम्
अभिचारिकमत्यर्थं त्रयस्त्रिंशच्छुभाक्षरम् ॥
1.17.m: the black Atharvan mantra, endowed with eight kalās, / highly potent for sorcery, having thirty-three auspicious syllables;

1.17.s:
yajurvedasamāyuktaṃ pañcatriṃśacchubhākṣaram
kalāṣṭakasamāyuktaṃ suśvetaṃ śāntikaṃ tathā //
1.17.d:
यजुर्वेदसमायुक्तं पञ्चत्रिंशच्छुभाक्षरम्
कलाष्टकसमायुक्तं सुश्वेतं शान्तिकं तथा ॥
1.17.m: and that associated with the Yajurveda, having thirty-five auspicious syllables, / endowed with eight kalās, pure white, and performing appeasement.

1.17.s:
trayodaśakalāyuktaṃ bālādyaiḥ saha lohitam
sāmodbhavaṃ jagatyādyaṃ vṛddhisaṃhārakāraṇam //
1.17.d:
त्रयोदशकलायुक्तं बालाद्यैः सह लोहितम्
सामोद्भवं जगत्याद्यं वृद्धिसंहारकारणम् ॥
1.17.m: Endowed with thirteen kalās, red, together with Bālā and the others, / originated from the Sāmaveda, primal in the world, the cause of increase and dissolution;

1.17.s:
varṇāḥ ṣaḍadhikāḥ ṣaṣṭir asya mantravarasya tu
pañca mantrāṃs tathā labdhvā jajāpa bhagavān hariḥ //
1.17.d:
वर्णाः षडधिकाः षष्टिर् अस्य मन्त्रवरस्य तु
पञ्च मन्त्रांस् तथा लब्ध्वा जजाप भगवान् हरिः ॥
1.17.m:
The syllables of this supreme mantra were sixty-six.
Having thus received the five mantras, Lord Hari chanted [them].

1.17.s:
atha dṛṣṭvā kalāvarṇam ṛgyajuḥsāmarūpiṇam
īśānamīśamukuṭaṃ puruṣāsyaṃ purātanam //
1.17.d:
अथ दृष्ट्वा कलावर्णम् ऋग्यजुःसामरूपिणम्
ईशानमीशमुकुटं पुरुषास्यं पुरातनम् ॥
1.17.m:
Then, having seen [the Lord], whose phonemes are the kalās, whose form is the Ṛg, Yajus, and Sāma,
Īśāna, crowned by the Lord, ancient, with the face of Puruṣa,

1.17.s:
aghorahṛdayaṃ hṛdyaṃ vāmaguhyaṃ sadāśivam
sadyaḥ pādaṃ mahādevaṃ mahābhogīndrabhūṣaṇam //
1.17.d:
अघोरहृदयं हृद्यं वामगुह्यं सदाशिवम्
सद्यः पादं महादेवं महाभोगीन्द्रभूषणम् ॥
1.17.m:
with the heart of Aghora, charming, with the secret parts of Vāma, Sadāśiva,
with Sadyojāta as his feet, Mahādeva, adorned with the great lord of serpents,

1.17.s:
viśvataḥ pādavadanaṃ viśvato 'kṣikaraṃ śivam
brahmaṇo 'dhipatiṃ sargasthitisaṃhārakāraṇam //
1.17.d:
विश्वतः पादवदनं विश्वतो ऽक्षिकरं शिवम्
ब्रह्मणो ऽधिपतिं सर्गस्थितिसंहारकारणम् ॥
1.17.m:
having feet and faces on every side, having eyes and hands on every side, Śiva,
the sovereign of Brahman, the cause of creation, maintenance, and dissolution,

1.17.s: tuṣṭāva punariṣṭābhir vāgbhir varadamīśvaram //
1.17.d: तुष्टाव पुनरिष्टाभिर् वाग्भिर् वरदमीश्वरम् ॥
1.17.m: he praised the boon-granting Lord again with pleasing words.

1.18.s:
viṣṇur uvāca
ekākṣarāya rudrāya akārāyātmarūpiṇe
ukārāyādidevāya vidyādehāya vai namaḥ //
1.18.d:
विष्णुर् उवाच
एकाक्षराय रुद्राय अकारायात्मरूपिणे
उकारायादिदेवाय विद्यादेहाय वै नमः ॥
1.18.m:
Viṣṇu said:
“Obeisance to Rudra of the single syllable, to the letter ‘A’, whose form is the Self,
to the letter ‘U’, the primeval deity, whose body is knowledge!

1.18.s:
tṛtīyāya makārāya śivāya paramātmane
sūryāgnisomavarṇāya yajamānāya vai namaḥ //
1.18.d:
तृतीयाय मकाराय शिवाय परमात्मने
सूर्याग्निसोमवर्णाय यजमानाय वै नमः ॥
1.18.m:
Obeisance to the third, the letter ‘M’, to Śiva, the Supreme Self,
whose complexion is that of the sun, fire, and moon, to the sacrificer!

1.18.s:
agnaye rudrarūpāya rudrāṇāṃ pataye namaḥ
śivāya śivamantrāya sadyojātāya vedhase //
1.18.d:
अग्नये रुद्ररूपाय रुद्राणां पतये नमः
शिवाय शिवमन्त्राय सद्योजाताय वेधसे ॥
1.18.m:
Obeisance to fire in the form of Rudra, obeisance to the lord of the Rudras,
to Śiva, the mantra of Śiva, to Sadyojāta, the creator!

1.18.s:
vāmāya vāmadevāya varadāyāmṛtāya te
aghorāyātighorāya sadyojātāya raṃhase //
1.18.d:
वामाय वामदेवाय वरदायामृताय ते
अघोरायातिघोराय सद्योजाताय रंहसे ॥
1.18.m:
To Vāma, to Vāmadeva, the giver of boons, to you who are nectar,
to Aghora, to the exceedingly terrible, to Sadyojāta, to speed!

1.18.s:
īśānāya śmaśānāya ativegāya vegine
namo 'stu śrutipādāya ūrdhvaliṅgāya liṅgine //
1.18.d:
ईशानाय श्मशानाय अतिवेगाय वेगिने
नमो ऽस्तु श्रुतिपादाय ऊर्ध्वलिङ्गाय लिङ्गिने ॥
1.18.m:
To Īśāna, to the cremation ground, to swift motion, to the swift one,
let there be obeisance to him whose feet are the Vedas, who has an erect liṅga, who possesses the liṅga!

1.18.s:
hemaliṅgāya hemāya vāriliṅgāya cāṃbhase
śivāya śivaliṅgāya vyāpine vyomavyāpine //
1.18.d:
हेमलिङ्गाय हेमाय वारिलिङ्गाय चांभसे
शिवाय शिवलिङ्गाय व्यापिने व्योमव्यापिने ॥
1.18.m:
To the golden liṅga, to gold, to the water liṅga and to water,
to Śiva, to the Śiva-liṅga, to the all-pervading, to the space-pervading!

1.18.s:
vāyave vāyuvegāya namaste vāyuvyāpine
tejase tejasāṃ bhartre namastejo 'dhivyāpine //
1.18.d:
वायवे वायुवेगाय नमस्ते वायुव्यापिने
तेजसे तेजसां भर्त्रे नमस्तेजो ऽधिव्यापिने ॥
1.18.m:
To the wind, having the speed of the wind, obeisance to you who pervade the wind;
to fire, to the maintainer of splendours, obeisance to you who supremely pervade light!

1.18.s:
jalāya jalabhūtāya namaste jalavyāpine
pṛthivyai cāntarikṣāya pṛthivīvyāpine namaḥ //
1.18.d:
जलाय जलभूताय नमस्ते जलव्यापिने
पृथिव्यै चान्तरिक्षाय पृथिवीव्यापिने नमः ॥
1.18.m:
To water, to him who has become water, obeisance to you who pervade water;
to the earth and to the atmosphere, obeisance to him who pervades the earth!

1.18.s:
śabdasparśasvarūpāya rasagandhāya gandhine
gaṇādhipataye tubhyaṃ guhyādguhyatamāya te //
1.18.d:
शब्दस्पर्शस्वरूपाय रसगन्धाय गन्धिने
गणाधिपतये तुभ्यं गुह्याद्गुह्यतमाय ते ॥
1.18.m:
To him whose nature is sound and touch, to taste and smell, to the fragrant one,
to the lord of the Gaṇas, to you, the most secret of secrets!

1.18.s:
anantāya virūpāya anantānāmayāya ca
śāśvatāya variṣṭhāya vārigarbhāya yogine //
1.18.d:
अनन्ताय विरूपाय अनन्तानामयाय च
शाश्वताय वरिष्ठाय वारिगर्भाय योगिने ॥
1.18.m:
To the infinite, to the multi-formed, and to the endless, healthy one,
to the eternal, the supreme, the water-wombed, the yogin,

1.18.s:
saṃsthitāyāmbhasāṃ madhye āvayormadhyavarcase
goptre hartre sadā kartre nidhanāyeśvarāya ca //
1.18.d:
संस्थितायाम्भसां मध्ये आवयोर्मध्यवर्चसे
गोप्त्रे हर्त्रे सदा कर्त्रे निधनायेश्वराय च ॥
1.18.m:
to him who stands in the midst of the waters, whose splendour is between the two of us,
to the protector, the destroyer, the perpetual creator, to the termination and to the Lord,

1.18.s:
acetanāya cintyāya cetanāyāsahāriṇe
arūpāya surūpāya anaṅgāyāṅgahāriṇe //
1.18.d:
अचेतनाय चिन्त्याय चेतनायासहारिणे
अरूपाय सुरूपाय अनङ्गायाङ्गहारिणे ॥
1.18.m:
to the inanimate, to the object of contemplation, to consciousness, to the destroyer of the unyielding,
to the formless, the beautiful-formed, the bodiless, the remover of bodies,

1.18.s:
bhasmadigdhaśarīrāya bhānusomāgnihetave
śvetāya śvetavarṇāya tuhinādricarāya ca //
1.18.d:
भस्मदिग्धशरीराय भानुसोमाग्निहेतवे
श्वेताय श्वेतवर्णाय तुहिनाद्रिचराय च ॥
1.18.m:
whose body is smeared with sacred ash, to the cause of the sun, moon, and fire,
to the white one, white-complexioned, and wanderer on the snowy mountain!

1.18.s:
suśvetāya suvaktrāya namaḥ śvetaśikhāya ca
śvetāsyāya mahāsyāya namaste śvetalohita //
1.18.d:
सुश्वेताय सुवक्त्राय नमः श्वेतशिखाय च
श्वेतास्याय महास्याय नमस्ते श्वेतलोहित ॥
1.18.m:
To the purely white, the fair-faced, obeisance to the white-crested one,
to the white-faced, the large-faced, obeisance to you, O white and red one!

1.18.s:
sutārāya viśiṣṭāya namo dundubhine hara
śatarūpavirūpāya namaḥ ketumate sadā //
1.18.d:
सुताराय विशिष्टाय नमो दुन्दुभिने हर
शतरूपविरूपाय नमः केतुमते सदा ॥
1.18.m:
To Sutāra, the distinguished, obeisance to the drum-bearer, O Hara;
to him of a hundred forms and diverse forms, obeisance always to the banner-bearer!

1.18.s:
ṛddhiśokaviśokāya pinākāya kapardine
vipāśāya supāśāya namaste pāśanāśine //
1.18.d:
ऋद्धिशोकविशोकाय पिनाकाय कपर्दिने
विपाशाय सुपाशाय नमस्ते पाशनाशिने ॥
1.18.m:
To him of prosperity, sorrow, and sorrowlessness, to Pināka, to the matted-haired one,
to the bondless, the well-bound, obeisance to you, the destroyer of bonds!

1.18.s:
suhotrāya haviṣyāya subrahmaṇyāya sūriṇe
sumukhāya suvaktrāya durdamāya damāya ca //
1.18.d:
सुहोत्राय हविष्याय सुब्रह्मण्याय सूरिणे
सुमुखाय सुवक्त्राय दुर्दमाय दमाय च ॥
1.18.m:
To Suhotra, the sacrificial offering, to Subrahmaṇya, the wise one,
to the fair-faced, the handsome-mouthed, to the hard to tame, and to restraint!

1.18.s:
kaṅkāya kaṅkarūpāya kaṅkaṇīkṛtapannaga
sanakāya namastubhyaṃ sanātana sanandana //
1.18.d:
कङ्काय कङ्करूपाय कङ्कणीकृतपन्नग
सनकाय नमस्तुभ्यं सनातन सनन्दन ॥
1.18.m:
To Kaṅka, in the form of Kaṅka, O you who have made serpents your bracelets!
Obeisance to you, O Sanaka, O eternal one, O Sanandana,

1.18.s:
sanatkumārasāraṅgam āraṇāya mahātmane
lokākṣiṇe tridhāmāya namo virajase sadā //
1.18.d:
सनत्कुमारसारङ्गम् आरणाय महात्मने
लोकाक्षिणे त्रिधामाय नमो विरजसे सदा ॥
1.18.m:
O Sanatkumāra, O Sāraṅga, to the slayer, the Great Self,
to the eye of the worlds, to him of three abodes, obeisance always to the passionless!

1.18.s:
śaṅkhapālāya śaṅkhāya rajase tamase namaḥ
sārasvatāya meghāya meghavāhana te namaḥ //
1.18.d:
शङ्खपालाय शङ्खाय रजसे तमसे नमः
सारस्वताय मेघाय मेघवाहन ते नमः ॥
1.18.m:
To Śaṅkhapāla, to Śaṅkha, to rajas and tamas, obeisance;
to Sārasvata, to the cloud, O you who ride on clouds, obeisance to you!

1.18.s:
suvāhāya vivāhāya vivādavaradāya ca
namaḥ śivāya rudrāya pradhānāya namonamaḥ //
1.18.d:
सुवाहाय विवाहाय विवादवरदाय च
नमः शिवाय रुद्राय प्रधानाय नमोनमः ॥
1.18.m:
To the easy bearer, to marriage, and to the granter of boons in disputes,
obeisance to Śiva, to Rudra, obeisance, obeisance to Pradhāna!

1.18.s:
triguṇāya namastubhyaṃ caturvyūhātmane namaḥ
saṃsārāya namastubhyaṃ namaḥ saṃsārahetave //
1.18.d:
त्रिगुणाय नमस्तुभ्यं चतुर्व्यूहात्मने नमः
संसाराय नमस्तुभ्यं नमः संसारहेतवे ॥
1.18.m:
Obeisance to you of the three guṇas, obeisance to the Self of the four manifestations,
obeisance to you who are worldly existence, obeisance to the cause of worldly existence!

1.18.s:
mokṣāya mokṣarūpāya mokṣakartre namonamaḥ
ātmane ṛṣaye tubhyaṃ svāmine viṣṇave namaḥ //
1.18.d:
मोक्षाय मोक्षरूपाय मोक्षकर्त्रे नमोनमः
आत्मने ऋषये तुभ्यं स्वामिने विष्णवे नमः ॥
1.18.m:
To liberation, the embodiment of liberation, obeisance, obeisance to the author of liberation;
to the Self, the seer, to you, the master, obeisance to Viṣṇu!

1.18.s:
namo bhagavate tubhyaṃ nāgānāṃ pataye namaḥ
oṅkārāya namastubhyaṃ sarvajñāya namo namaḥ //
1.18.d:
नमो भगवते तुभ्यं नागानां पतये नमः
ओङ्काराय नमस्तुभ्यं सर्वज्ञाय नमो नमः ॥
1.18.m:
Obeisance to you, the Lord, obeisance to the ruler of serpents;
obeisance to you who are the Oṃkāra, obeisance, obeisance to the omniscient one!

1.18.s:
sarvāya ca namastubhyaṃ namo nārāyaṇāya ca
namo hiraṇyagarbhāya ādidevāya te namaḥ //
1.18.d:
सर्वाय च नमस्तुभ्यं नमो नारायणाय च
नमो हिरण्यगर्भाय आदिदेवाय ते नमः ॥
1.18.m:
Obeisance to Sarva, and obeisance to Nārāyaṇa;
obeisance to Hiraṇyagarbha, obeisance to you, the primeval deity!

1.18.s:
namo 'stvajāya pataye prajānāṃ vyūhahetave
mahādevāya devānām īśvarāya namo namaḥ //
1.18.d:
नमो ऽस्त्वजाय पतये प्रजानां व्यूहहेतवे
महादेवाय देवानाम् ईश्वराय नमो नमः ॥
1.18.m:
Let obeisance be to the unborn, the master of creatures, the cause of cosmic arrangement;
obeisance, obeisance to Mahādeva, the sovereign of the gods!

1.18.s:
śarvāya ca namastubhyaṃ satyāya śamanāya ca
brahmaṇe caiva bhūtānāṃ sarvajñāya namo namaḥ //
1.18.d:
शर्वाय च नमस्तुभ्यं सत्याय शमनाय च
ब्रह्मणे चैव भूतानां सर्वज्ञाय नमो नमः ॥
1.18.m:
Obeisance to you, O Śarva, to truth, and to the pacifier;
to Brahman and to the omniscient one of beings, obeisance, obeisance!

1.18.s:
mahātmane namastubhyaṃ prajñārūpāya vai namaḥ
citaye citirūpāya smṛtirūpāya vai namaḥ //
1.18.d:
महात्मने नमस्तुभ्यं प्रज्ञारूपाय वै नमः
चितये चितिरूपाय स्मृतिरूपाय वै नमः ॥
1.18.m:
Obeisance to you, the Great Self, obeisance to the embodiment of wisdom;
to consciousness, to the embodiment of consciousness, obeisance to the embodiment of memory!

1.18.s:
jñānāya jñānagamyāya namaste saṃvide sadā
śikharāya namastubhyaṃ nīlakaṇṭhāya vai namaḥ //
1.18.d:
ज्ञानाय ज्ञानगम्याय नमस्ते संविदे सदा
शिखराय नमस्तुभ्यं नीलकण्ठाय वै नमः ॥
1.18.m:
To knowledge, to him who is attained by knowledge, obeisance always to you, pure awareness;
obeisance to you, the peak, obeisance indeed to the blue-throated one!

1.18.s:
ardhanārīśarīrāya avyaktāya namonamaḥ
ekādaśavibhedāya sthāṇave te namaḥ sadā //
1.18.d:
अर्धनारीशरीराय अव्यक्ताय नमोनमः
एकादशविभेदाय स्थाणवे ते नमः सदा ॥
1.18.m:
To him whose body is half woman, to the unmanifest, obeisance, obeisance;
to him of eleven divisions, obeisance always to you, the immovable pillar!

1.18.s:
namaḥ somāya sūryāya bhavāya bhavahāriṇe
yaśaskarāya devāya śaṅkarāyeśvarāya ca //
1.18.d:
नमः सोमाय सूर्याय भवाय भवहारिणे
यशस्कराय देवाय शङ्करायेश्वराय च ॥
1.18.m:
Obeisance to Soma, to the sun, to Bhava, to the remover of worldly existence,
to the fame-giving deity, to Śaṅkara and to the Lord!

1.18.s:
namo 'ṃbikādhipataye umāyāḥ pataye namaḥ
hiraṇyabāhave tubhyaṃ namaste hemaretase //
1.18.d:
नमो ऽंबिकाधिपतये उमायाः पतये नमः
हिरण्यबाहवे तुभ्यं नमस्ते हेमरेतसे ॥
1.18.m:
Obeisance to the lord of Ambikā, obeisance to the consort of Umā;
to you of golden arms, obeisance to you whose seed is gold!

1.18.s:
nīlakeśāya vittāya śitikaṇṭhāya vai namaḥ
kapardine namastubhyaṃ nāgāṅgābharaṇāya ca //
1.18.d:
नीलकेशाय वित्ताय शितिकण्ठाय वै नमः
कपर्दिने नमस्तुभ्यं नागाङ्गाभरणाय च ॥
1.18.m:
To the blue-haired, the wealthy, obeisance indeed to the dark-necked one;
obeisance to you of matted hair, and to him whose ornaments are serpents’ limbs!

1.18.s:
vṛṣārūḍhāya sarvasya hartre kartre namonamaḥ
vīrarāmātirāmāya rāmanāthāya te vibho //
1.18.d:
वृषारूढाय सर्वस्य हर्त्रे कर्त्रे नमोनमः
वीररामातिरामाय रामनाथाय ते विभो ॥
1.18.m:
To him who rides the bull, to the destroyer and creator of all, obeisance, obeisance;
to the hero Rāma, the supreme Rāma, to you, the protector Rāma, O all-pervading one!

1.18.s:
namo rājādhirājāya rājñāmadhigatāya te
namaḥ pālādhipataye pālāśākṛntate namaḥ //
1.18.d:
नमो राजाधिराजाय राज्ञामधिगताय ते
नमः पालाधिपतये पालाशाकृन्तते नमः ॥
1.18.m:
Obeisance to the king of kings, to you who are attained by kings;
obeisance to the protector of guardians, obeisance to the cutter of the foliage!

1.18.s:
namaḥ keyūrabhūṣāya gopate te namonamaḥ
namaḥ śrīkaṇṭhanāthāya namo likucapāṇaye //
1.18.d:
नमः केयूरभूषाय गोपते ते नमोनमः
नमः श्रीकण्ठनाथाय नमो लिकुचपाणये ॥
1.18.m:
Obeisance to him adorned with armlets, to the lord of cattle, obeisance, obeisance to you;
obeisance to the lord Śrīkaṇṭha, obeisance to him with a lime fruit in his hand!

1.18.s:
bhuvaneśāya devāya vedaśāstra namo 'stu te
sāraṅgāya namastubhyaṃ rājahaṃsāya te namaḥ //
1.18.d:
भुवनेशाय देवाय वेदशास्त्र नमो ऽस्तु ते
सारङ्गाय नमस्तुभ्यं राजहंसाय ते नमः ॥
1.18.m:
To the Lord of the world, to the god, O you whose treatises are the Vedas, let obeisance be to you;
obeisance to you, the cātake bird, obeisance to you, the royal swan!

1.18.s:
kanakāṅgadahārāya namaḥ sarpopavītine
sarpakuṇḍalamālāya kaṭisūtrīkṛtāhine //
1.18.d:
कनकाङ्गदहाराय नमः सर्पोपवीतिने
सर्पकुण्डलमालाय कटिसूत्रीकृताहिने ॥
1.18.m:
To him with a necklace of golden bracelets, obeisance to him whose sacred thread is a serpent,
who has garlands of serpent earrings, who has made a snake his waist-thread!

1.18.s:
vedagarbhāya garbhāya viśvagarbhāya te śiva
virarāmeti saṃstutvā brahmaṇā sahito hariḥ //
1.18.d:
वेदगर्भाय गर्भाय विश्वगर्भाय ते शिव
विररामेति संस्तुत्वा ब्रह्मणा सहितो हरिः ॥
1.18.m:
To you, the womb of the Vedas, the embryo, the womb of the universe, O Śiva!”
Having praised him thus together with Brahmā, Hari paused.

1.18.s:
etatstotravaraṃ puṇyaṃ sarvapāpapraṇāśanam
yaḥ paṭhecchrāvayedvāpi brāhmaṇān vedapāragān //
1.18.d:
एतत्स्तोत्रवरं पुण्यं सर्वपापप्रणाशनम्
यः पठेच्छ्रावयेद्वापि ब्राह्मणान् वेदपारगान् ॥
1.18.m:
Whoever recites this excellent, sacred hymn that destroys all sins,
or causes it to be heard by Brāhmaṇas who have mastered the Vedas,

1.18.s:
sa yāti brahmaṇo loke pāpakarmarato 'pi vai
tasmājjapetpaṭhennityaṃ śrāvayedbrāhmaṇāñchubhān //
1.18.d:
स याति ब्रह्मणो लोके पापकर्मरतो ऽपि वै
तस्माज्जपेत्पठेन्नित्यं श्रावयेद्ब्राह्मणाञ्छुभान् ॥
1.18.m:
goes to the world of Brahmā, even if devoted to sinful deeds.
Therefore, one should constantly recite, study, and cause auspicious Brāhmaṇas to hear [it],

1.18.s: sarvapāpaviśuddhyarthaṃ viṣṇunā paribhāṣitam //
1.18.d: सर्वपापविशुद्ध्यर्थं विष्णुना परिभाषितम् ॥
1.18.m: for the sake of purification from all sins, as spoken by Viṣṇu.

1.19.s:
sūta uvāca
athovāca mahādevaḥ prīto 'haṃ surasattamau
paśyatāṃ māṃ mahādevaṃ bhayaṃ sarvaṃ vimucyatām //
1.19.d:
सूत उवाच
अथोवाच महादेवः प्रीतो ऽहं सुरसत्तमौ
पश्यतां मां महादेवं भयं सर्वं विमुच्यताम् ॥
1.19.m:
Sūta said:
Then Mahādeva said: “I am pleased, O best of gods!
Behold me, Mahādeva; let all fear be cast away!

1.19.s:
yuvāṃ prasūtau gātrābhyāṃ mama pūrvaṃ mahābalau
ayaṃ me dakṣiṇe pārśve brahmā lokapitāmahaḥ //
1.19.d:
युवां प्रसूतौ गात्राभ्यां मम पूर्वं महाबलौ
अयं मे दक्षिणे पार्श्वे ब्रह्मा लोकपितामहः ॥
1.19.m:
The two of you were born from my limbs of old, O exceedingly powerful ones:
this Brahmā, the grandfather of the worlds, is on my right side;

1.19.s:
vāme pārśve ca me viṣṇur viśvātmā hṛdayodbhavaḥ
prīto 'haṃ yuvayoḥ samyag varaṃ dadmi yathepsitam //
1.19.d:
वामे पार्श्वे च मे विष्णुर् विश्वात्मा हृदयोद्भवः
प्रीतो ऽहं युवयोः सम्यग् वरं दद्मि यथेप्सितम् ॥
1.19.m:
and on my left side is Viṣṇu, the soul of the universe, born from my heart.
I am thoroughly pleased with both of you; I grant a boon as desired.”

1.19.s:
evamuktvā tu taṃ viṣṇuṃ karābhyāṃ parameśvaraḥ
pasparśa subhagābhyāṃ tu kṛpayā tu kṛpānidhiḥ //
1.19.d:
एवमुक्त्वा तु तं विष्णुं कराभ्यां परमेश्वरः
पस्पर्श सुभगाभ्यां तु कृपया तु कृपानिधिः ॥
1.19.m:
Having spoken thus, the Supreme Lord, a treasure of compassion, touched that Viṣṇu
with both auspicious hands out of grace.

1.19.s:
tataḥ prahṛṣṭamanasā praṇipatya maheśvaram
prāha nārāyaṇo nāthaṃ liṅgasthaṃ liṅgavarjitam //
1.19.d:
ततः प्रहृष्टमनसा प्रणिपत्य महेश्वरम्
प्राह नारायणो नाथं लिङ्गस्थं लिङ्गवर्जितम् ॥
1.19.m:
Then, bowing down to Maheśvara with an exultant mind,
Nārāyaṇa spoke to the master who abides in the liṅga and is devoid of a liṅga:

1.19.s:
yadi prītiḥ samutpannā yadi deyo varaś ca nau
bhaktirbhavatu nau nityaṃ tvayi cāvyabhicāriṇī //
1.19.d:
यदि प्रीतिः समुत्पन्ना यदि देयो वरश् च नौ
भक्तिर्भवतु नौ नित्यं त्वयि चाव्यभिचारिणी ॥
1.19.m:
“If affection has arisen, and if a boon is to be given to both of us,
may there always be unwavering devotion in both of us toward you.”

1.19.s:
devaḥ pradattavān devāḥ svātmanyavyabhicāriṇīm
brahmaṇe viṣṇave caiva śraddhāṃ śītāṃśubhūṣaṇaḥ //
1.19.d:
देवः प्रदत्तवान् देवाः स्वात्मन्यव्यभिचारिणीम्
ब्रह्मणे विष्णवे चैव श्रद्धां शीतांशुभूषणः ॥
1.19.m: The god adorned with the cool-rayed moon granted to Brahmā / and to Viṣṇu unswerving faith directed toward himself, O gods.

1.19.s:
jānubhyāmavanīṃ gatvā punarnārāyaṇaḥ svayam
praṇipatya ca viśveśaṃ prāha mandataraṃ vaśī //
1.19.d:
जानुभ्यामवनीं गत्वा पुनर्नारायणः स्वयम्
प्रणिपत्य च विश्वेशं प्राह मन्दतरं वशी ॥
1.19.m: Falling to the earth upon his knees, Nārāyaṇa himself, / having bowed to the lord of all, the self-controlled one spoke very softly:

1.19.s:
āvayordevadeveśa vivādamatiśobhanam
ihāgato bhavān yasmād vivādaśamanāya nau //
1.19.d:
आवयोर्देवदेवेश विवादमतिशोभनम्
इहागतो भवान् यस्माद् विवादशमनाय नौ ॥
1.19.m: “O lord of the gods of gods, our dispute has turned out very auspicious, / since you have arrived here to pacify the dispute between us two.”

1.19.s:
tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā punaḥ prāha haro harim
praṇipatya sthitaṃ mūrdhnā kṛtāñjalipuṭaṃ smayan //
1.19.d:
तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा पुनः प्राह हरो हरिम्
प्रणिपत्य स्थितं मूर्ध्ना कृताञ्जलिपुटं स्मयन् ॥
1.19.m: Hearing those words of his, Hara spoke again to Hari, / who stood with his head bowed and hands folded in supplication, smiling [as he spoke]:

1.19.s:
śrīmahādeva uvāca
pralayasthitisargāṇāṃ kartā tvaṃ dharaṇīpate
vatsa vatsa hare viṣṇo pālayaitaccarācaram //
1.19.d:
श्रीमहादेव उवाच
प्रलयस्थितिसर्गाणां कर्ता त्वं धरणीपते
वत्स वत्स हरे विष्णो पालयैतच्चराचरम् ॥
1.19.m: The venerable Mahādeva said: / “You are the maker of cosmic dissolution, maintenance, and creation, O lord of the earth! / Dear child, dear child, O Hari, O Viṣṇu, protect this moving and unmoving world!

1.19.s:
tridhā bhinno hyahaṃ viṣṇo brahmaviṣṇubhavākhyayā
sargarakṣālayaguṇair niṣkalaḥ parameśvaraḥ //
1.19.d:
त्रिधा भिन्नो ह्यहं विष्णो ब्रह्मविष्णुभवाख्यया
सर्गरक्षालयगुणैर् निष्कलः परमेश्वरः ॥
1.19.m: For I, the partless Supreme Lord, am differentiated threefold, O Viṣṇu, / under the names of Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Bhava, through the guṇas of creation, protection, and dissolution.

1.19.s:
saṃmohaṃ tyaja bho viṣṇo pālayainaṃ pitāmaham
pādme bhaviṣyati sutaḥ kalpe tava pitāmahaḥ //
1.19.d:
संमोहं त्यज भो विष्णो पालयैनं पितामहम्
पाद्मे भविष्यति सुतः कल्पे तव पितामहः ॥
1.19.m: Cast off delusion, O Viṣṇu! Protect this Pitāmaha. / In the Pādma kalpa, Pitāmaha shall become your son.

1.19.s:
tadā drakṣyasi māṃ caivaṃ so 'pi drakṣyati padmajaḥ
evamuktvā sa bhagavāṃs tatraivāntaradhīyata //
1.19.d:
तदा द्रक्ष्यसि मां चैवं सो ऽपि द्रक्ष्यति पद्मजः
एवमुक्त्वा स भगवांस् तत्रैवान्तरधीयत ॥
1.19.m: Then you shall see me thus, and he too, born of the lotus, shall see [me].” / Having spoken thus, the Lord vanished right there.

1.19.s:
tadāprabhṛti lokeṣu liṅgārcā supratiṣṭhitā
liṅgavedī mahādevī liṅgaṃ sākṣānmaheśvaraḥ //
1.19.d:
तदाप्रभृति लोकेषु लिङ्गार्चा सुप्रतिष्ठिता
लिङ्गवेदी महादेवी लिङ्गं साक्षान्महेश्वरः ॥
1.19.m: From that time forward, worship of the liṅga was firmly established in the worlds: / the pedestal of the liṅga is the Great Goddess, and the liṅga is Maheśvara manifest.

1.19.s:
layanālliṅgamityuktaṃ tatraiva nikhilaṃ surāḥ
yastu laiṅgaṃ paṭhennityam ākhyānaṃ liṅgasannidhau //
1.19.d:
लयनाल्लिङ्गमित्युक्तं तत्रैव निखिलं सुराः
यस्तु लैङ्गं पठेन्नित्यम् आख्यानं लिङ्गसन्निधौ ॥
1.19.m: It is called ‘liṅga’ because of dissolution (laya); everything [dissolves] into it, O gods. / Whoever constantly recites this narrative pertaining to the liṅga in the presence of a liṅga—

1.19.s: sa yāti śivatāṃ vipro nātra kāryā vicāraṇā //
1.19.d: स याति शिवतां विप्रो नात्र कार्या विचारणा ॥
1.19.m: that brāhmaṇa attains the state of Śiva; no doubt should be entertained on this point.

1.20.s:
ṛṣaya ūcuḥ
kathaṃ pādme purā kalpe brahmā padmodbhavo 'bhavat
bhavaṃ ca dṛṣṭavāṃstena brahmaṇā puruṣottamaḥ //
1.20.d:
ऋषय ऊचुः
कथं पाद्मे पुरा कल्पे ब्रह्मा पद्मोद्भवो ऽभवत्
भवं च दृष्टवांस्तेन ब्रह्मणा पुरुषोत्तमः ॥
1.20.m: The ṛṣis said: / “How did Brahmā become lotus-born in the ancient Pādma kalpa, / and [how] did Puruṣottama see Bhava together with that Brahmā?

1.20.s:
etatsarvaṃ viśeṣeṇa sāṃprataṃ vaktumarhasi
āsīdekārṇavaṃ ghoram avibhāgaṃ tamomayam //
1.20.d:
एतत्सर्वं विशेषेण सांप्रतं वक्तुमर्हसि
आसीदेकार्णवं घोरम् अविभागं तमोमयम् ॥
1.20.m: You ought to tell all this in detail now.” / [The Sūta said:] “There was a single, dreadful, undifferentiated ocean, full of darkness.

1.20.s:
madhye caikārṇave tasmin śaṅkhacakragadādharaḥ
jīmūtābho 'mbujākṣaś ca kirīṭī śrīpatirhariḥ //
1.20.d:
मध्ये चैकार्णवे तस्मिन् शङ्खचक्रगदाधरः
जीमूताभो ऽम्बुजाक्षश् च किरीटी श्रीपतिर्हरिः ॥
1.20.m: And in the midst of that single ocean was Hari, the bearer of the conch, discus, and mace, / resembling a cloud, lotus-eyed, diademed, the lord of Śrī,

1.20.s:
nārāyaṇamukhodgīrṇasarvātmā puruṣottamaḥ
aṣṭabāhurmahāvakṣā lokānāṃ yonirucyate //
1.20.d:
नारायणमुखोद्गीर्णसर्वात्मा पुरुषोत्तमः
अष्टबाहुर्महावक्षा लोकानां योनिरुच्यते ॥
1.20.m: Puruṣottama, the self of all, uttered from the mouth of Nārāyaṇa, / eight-armed, broad-chested, said to be the source of the worlds.

1.20.s:
kimapyacintyaṃ yogātmā yogamāsthāya yogavit
phaṇāsahasrakalitaṃ tamapratimavarcasam //
1.20.d:
किमप्यचिन्त्यं योगात्मा योगमास्थाय योगवित्
फणासहस्रकलितं तमप्रतिमवर्चसम् ॥
1.20.m: Having resorted to an inconceivable yoga, he who has yoga as his self, the knower of yoga, / [prepared] the body endowed with a thousand hoods, of matchless radiance,

1.20.s:
mahābhogapaterbhogaṃ sādhvāstīrya mahocchrayam
tasminmahati paryaṅke śete caikārṇave prabhuḥ //
1.20.d:
महाभोगपतेर्भोगं साध्वास्तीर्य महोच्छ्रयम्
तस्मिन्महति पर्यङ्के शेते चैकार्णवे प्रभुः ॥
1.20.m: having properly spread out the immensely lofty coils of the lord of great serpent-coils; / on that great couch the Lord was lying in the single ocean.

1.20.s:
evaṃ tatra śayānena viṣṇunā prabhaviṣṇunā
ātmārāmeṇa krīḍārthaṃ līlayākliṣṭakarmaṇā //
1.20.d:
एवं तत्र शयानेन विष्णुना प्रभविष्णुना
आत्मारामेण क्रीडार्थं लीलयाक्लिष्टकर्मणा ॥
1.20.m: Thus, while lying there, by the all-powerful Viṣṇu, / who delights in the self, for the sake of sport, effortlessly in divine play,

1.20.s:
śatayojanavistīrṇaṃ taruṇādityasannibham
vajradaṇḍaṃ mahotsedhaṃ nābhyāṃ sṛṣṭaṃ tu puṣkaram //
1.20.d:
शतयोजनविस्तीर्णं तरुणादित्यसन्निभम्
वज्रदण्डं महोत्सेधं नाभ्यां सृष्टं तु पुष्करम् ॥
1.20.m: a lotus was created from his navel, extending a hundred yojanas, / resembling the morning sun, with a stalk of diamond, and of great height.

1.20.s:
tasyaivaṃ krīḍamānasya samīpaṃ devamīḍhuṣaḥ
hemagarbhāṇḍajo brahmā rukmavarṇo hyatīndriyaḥ //
1.20.d:
तस्यैवं क्रीडमानस्य समीपं देवमीढुषः
हेमगर्भाण्डजो ब्रह्मा रुक्मवर्णो ह्यतीन्द्रियः ॥
1.20.m: As he was sporting thus, near to the bounteous god / came Brahmā, born from the golden egg, gold-colored, beyond the senses,

1.20.s:
caturvaktro viśālākṣaḥ samāgamya yadṛcchayā
śriyā yuktena divyena suśubhena sugandhinā //
1.20.d:
चतुर्वक्त्रो विशालाक्षः समागम्य यदृच्छया
श्रिया युक्तेन दिव्येन सुशुभेन सुगन्धिना ॥
1.20.m: four-faced, large-eyed, having approached by chance, / [and] having seen [him] endowed with auspicious sight, sporting with the lotus

1.20.s:
krīḍamānaṃ ca padmena dṛṣṭvā brahmā śubhekṣaṇam
savismayamathāgamya saumyasampannayā girā //
1.20.d:
क्रीडमानं च पद्मेन दृष्ट्वा ब्रह्मा शुभेक्षणम्
सविस्मयमथागम्य सौम्यसम्पन्नया गिरा ॥
1.20.m: endowed with splendor, divine, very auspicious, and fragrant; / then, having approached with wonder, Brahmā with gentle and gracious speech

1.20.s:
provāca ko bhavāñchete hy āśrito madhyamambhasām
atha tasyācyutaḥ śrutvā brahmaṇastu śubhaṃ vacaḥ //
1.20.d:
प्रोवाच को भवाञ्छेते ह्य् आश्रितो मध्यमम्भसाम्
अथ तस्याच्युतः श्रुत्वा ब्रह्मणस्तु शुभं वचः ॥
1.20.m: said: “Who are you, who lie here resting in the midst of the waters?” / Thereupon Acyuta, hearing that auspicious speech of Brahmā,

1.20.s:
udatiṣṭhata paryaṅkād vismayotphullalocanaḥ
pratyuvācottaraṃ caiva kalpe kalpe pratiśrayaḥ //
1.20.d:
उदतिष्ठत पर्यङ्काद् विस्मयोत्फुल्ललोचनः
प्रत्युवाचोत्तरं चैव कल्पे कल्पे प्रतिश्रयः ॥
1.20.m: arose from the couch, his eyes wide open with wonder, / and gave an answer, he who is the refuge kalpa after kalpa:

1.20.s:
kartavyaṃ ca kṛtaṃ caiva kriyate yacca kiṃcana
dyaurantarikṣaṃ bhūścaiva paraṃ padamahaṃ bhuvaḥ //
1.20.d:
कर्तव्यं च कृतं चैव क्रियते यच्च किंचन
द्यौरन्तरिक्षं भूश्चैव परं पदमहं भुवः ॥
1.20.m: “Whatever is to be done, whatever has been done, and whatever is being done, / the sky, the atmosphere, and the earth—I am the supreme realm of the earth.”

1.20.s:
tamevamuktvā bhagavān viṣṇuḥ punarathābravīt
kastvaṃ khalu samāyātaḥ samīpaṃ bhagavānkutaḥ //
1.20.d:
तमेवमुक्त्वा भगवान् विष्णुः पुनरथाब्रवीत्
कस्त्वं खलु समायातः समीपं भगवान्कुतः ॥
1.20.m: Having spoken thus to him, the blessed Viṣṇu spoke again: / “Who indeed are you, O venerable one, and whence have you come near?

1.20.s:
kva vā bhūyaś ca gantavyaṃ kaś ca vā te pratiśrayaḥ
ko bhavān viśvamūrtirvai kartavyaṃ kiṃ ca te mayā //
1.20.d:
क्व वा भूयश् च गन्तव्यं कश् च वा ते प्रतिश्रयः
को भवान् विश्वमूर्तिर्वै कर्तव्यं किं च ते मया ॥
1.20.m: Or where are you to go again, and what is your abode? / Who are you whose form is the universe, and what is to be done for you by me?”

1.20.s:
evaṃ bruvantaṃ vaikuṇṭhaṃ pratyuvāca pitāmahaḥ
māyayā mohitaḥ śaṃbhor avijñāya janārdanam //
1.20.d:
एवं ब्रुवन्तं वैकुण्ठं प्रत्युवाच पितामहः
मायया मोहितः शंभोर् अविज्ञाय जनार्दनम् ॥
1.20.m: To Vaikuṇṭha who was speaking thus, Pitāmaha replied, / deluded by the māyā of Śambhu, not recognizing Janārdana,

1.20.s:
māyayā mohitaṃ devam avijñātaṃ mahātmanaḥ
yathā bhavāṃstathaivāham ādikartā prajāpatiḥ //
1.20.d:
मायया मोहितं देवम् अविज्ञातं महात्मनः
यथा भवांस्तथैवाहम् आदिकर्ता प्रजापतिः ॥
1.20.m: the god who was deluded by māyā, unaware of the great-souled one: / “Just as you are, even so am I: the primeval creator, Prajāpati.”

1.20.s:
savismayaṃ vacaḥ śrutvā brahmaṇo lokatantriṇaḥ
anujñātaś ca te nātha vaikuṇṭho viśvasaṃbhavaḥ //
1.20.d:
सविस्मयं वचः श्रुत्वा ब्रह्मणो लोकतन्त्रिणः
अनुज्ञातश् च ते नाथ वैकुण्ठो विश्वसंभवः ॥
1.20.m: Hearing the wondrous words of Brahmā, the orchestrator of the worlds, / and permitted by you, O Lord, Vaikuṇṭha, the source of the universe,

1.20.s:
kautūhalānmahāyogī praviṣṭo brahmaṇo mukham
imānaṣṭādaśa dvīpān sasamudrān saparvatān //
1.20.d:
कौतूहलान्महायोगी प्रविष्टो ब्रह्मणो मुखम्
इमानष्टादश द्वीपान् ससमुद्रान् सपर्वतान् ॥
1.20.m: the great yogin out of curiosity entered the mouth of Brahmā. / Having entered these eighteen continents with their oceans and mountains,

1.20.s:
praviśya sumahātejāś cāturvarṇyasamākulān
brahmaṇastambhaparyantaṃ saptalokān sanātanān //
1.20.d:
प्रविश्य सुमहातेजाश् चातुर्वर्ण्यसमाकुलान्
ब्रह्मणस्तम्भपर्यन्तं सप्तलोकान् सनातनान् ॥
1.20.m: the one of very great splendor [beheld] them filled with the four social classes; / and seeing all the seven eternal worlds extending up to the world of Brahmā

1.20.s:
brahmaṇastūdare dṛṣṭvā sarvānviṣṇurmahābhujaḥ
aho 'sya tapaso vīryam ityuktvā ca punaḥ punaḥ //
1.20.d:
ब्रह्मणस्तूदरे दृष्ट्वा सर्वान्विष्णुर्महाभुजः
अहो ऽस्य तपसो वीर्यम् इत्युक्त्वा च पुनः पुनः ॥
1.20.m: within the belly of Brahmā, the mighty-armed Viṣṇu, / saying again and again, “Oh, the power of his ascetic practice!”,

1.20.s:
aṭitvā vividhāṃllokān viṣṇurnānāvidhāśrayān
tato varṣasahasrānte nāntaṃ hi dadṛśe yadā //
1.20.d:
अटित्वा विविधांल्लोकान् विष्णुर्नानाविधाश्रयान्
ततो वर्षसहस्रान्ते नान्तं हि ददृशे यदा ॥
1.20.m: wandered through the various worlds that served as diverse abodes; / and then, at the end of a thousand years, when he did not see an end,

1.20.s:
tadāsya vaktrānniṣkramya pannagendraniketanaḥ
nārāyaṇo jagaddhātā pitāmahamathābravīt //
1.20.d:
तदास्य वक्त्रान्निष्क्रम्य पन्नगेन्द्रनिकेतनः
नारायणो जगद्धाता पितामहमथाब्रवीत् ॥
1.20.m: then emerging from his mouth, Nārāyaṇa whose abode is the lord of serpents, / the maintainer of the world, then spoke to Pitāmaha:

1.20.s:
bhagavānādiraṅkaś ca madhyaṃ kālo diśo nabhaḥ
nāhamantaṃ prapaśyāmi udarasya tavānagha //
1.20.d:
भगवानादिरङ्कश् च मध्यं कालो दिशो नभः
नाहमन्तं प्रपश्यामि उदरस्य तवानघ ॥
1.20.m: “O venerable one, the beginning, the end, the middle, time, the directions, and space— / I do not see the end of your belly, O sinless one.”

1.20.s:
evamuktvābravīdbhūyaḥ pitāmahamidaṃ hariḥ
bhagavānevamevāhaṃ śāśvataṃ hi mamodaram //
1.20.d:
एवमुक्त्वाब्रवीद्भूयः पितामहमिदं हरिः
भगवानेवमेवाहं शाश्वतं हि ममोदरम् ॥
1.20.m: Having spoken thus, Hari spoke further to Pitāmaha: / “O venerable one, in the very same way is my belly eternal;

1.20.s:
praviśya lokān paśyaitān anaupamyānsurottama
tataḥ prāhlādinīṃ vāṇīṃ śrutvā tasyābhinandya ca //
1.20.d:
प्रविश्य लोकान् पश्यैतान् अनौपम्यान्सुरोत्तम
ततः प्राह्लादिनीं वाणीं श्रुत्वा तस्याभिनन्द्य च ॥
1.20.m: enter and behold these incomparable worlds, O best of gods!” / Thereupon, hearing his delightful words and applauding them,

1.20.s:
śrīpaterudaraṃ bhūyaḥ praviveśa pitāmahaḥ
tāneva lokān garbhasthān apaśyat satyavikramaḥ //
1.20.d:
श्रीपतेरुदरं भूयः प्रविवेश पितामहः
तानेव लोकान् गर्भस्थान् अपश्यत् सत्यविक्रमः ॥
1.20.m: Pitāmaha entered the belly of the lord of Śrī once more. / The one of true valor beheld those very same worlds situated within the belly.

1.20.s:
paryaṭitvā tu devasya dadṛśe 'ntaṃ na vai hareḥ
jñātvā gatiṃ tasya pitāmahasya dvārāṇi sarvāṇi pidhāya viṣṇuḥ
vibhurmanaḥ kartumiyeṣa cāśu sukhaṃ prasupto 'hamiti pracintya //
1.20.d:
पर्यटित्वा तु देवस्य ददृशे ऽन्तं न वै हरेः
ज्ञात्वा गतिं तस्य पितामहस्य द्वाराणि सर्वाणि पिधाय विष्णुः
विभुर्मनः कर्तुमियेष चाशु सुखं प्रसुप्तो ऽहमिति प्रचिन्त्य ॥
1.20.m: Having wandered about, he did not see the end of the god Hari. / Having realized that path of Pitāmaha, Viṣṇu closed all the gates; / the all-pervading lord quickly resolved in his mind, thinking: “I have gone comfortably to sleep.”

1.20.s:
tato dvārāṇi sarvāṇi pihitāni samīkṣya vai
sūkṣmaṃ kṛtvātmano rūpaṃ nābhyāṃ dvāramavindata //
1.20.d:
ततो द्वाराणि सर्वाणि पिहितानि समीक्ष्य वै
सूक्ष्मं कृत्वात्मनो रूपं नाभ्यां द्वारमविन्दत ॥
1.20.m: Then, seeing indeed all the gates closed, / having made his own form subtle, he found an opening in the navel.

1.20.s:
padmasūtrānusāreṇa cānvapaśyatpitāmahaḥ
ujjahārātmano rūpaṃ puṣkarāccaturānanaḥ //
1.20.d:
पद्मसूत्रानुसारेण चान्वपश्यत्पितामहः
उज्जहारात्मनो रूपं पुष्कराच्चतुराननः ॥
1.20.m: Following along the lotus stalk, Pitāmaha looked along it; / the four-faced one brought his own form out from the lotus.

1.20.s:
virarājāravindasthaḥ padmagarbhasamadyutiḥ
brahmā svayaṃbhūrbhagavāñ jagadyoniḥ pitāmahaḥ //
1.20.d:
विरराजारविन्दस्थः पद्मगर्भसमद्युतिः
ब्रह्मा स्वयंभूर्भगवाञ् जगद्योनिः पितामहः ॥
1.20.m: Resting upon the lotus, radiant as the inside of a lotus, / shone Brahmā, the self-born Lord, the womb of the universe, Pitāmaha.

1.20.s:
etasminnantare tābhyām ekaikasya tu kṛtsnaśaḥ
vartamāne tu saṃgharṣe madhye tasyārṇavasya tu //
1.20.d:
एतस्मिन्नन्तरे ताभ्याम् एकैकस्य तु कृत्स्नशः
वर्तमाने तु संघर्षे मध्ये तस्यार्णवस्य तु ॥
1.20.m: Meanwhile, as an encounter was taking place between the two of them / in which each was testing the other entirely in the midst of that ocean,

1.20.s:
kuto 'pyaparimeyātmā bhūtānāṃ prabhurīśvaraḥ
śūlapāṇirmahādevo hemavīrāṃbaracchadaḥ //
1.20.d:
कुतो ऽप्यपरिमेयात्मा भूतानां प्रभुरीश्वरः
शूलपाणिर्महादेवो हेमवीरांबरच्छदः ॥
1.20.m: from somewhere came the Lord, the ruler of beings, of immeasurable self, / Mahādeva, trident in hand, wearing garments of golden heroic cloth;

1.20.s:
agacchadyatra so 'nanto nāgabhogapatir hariḥ
śīghraṃ vikramatastasya padbhyām ākrāntapīḍitāḥ //
1.20.d:
अगच्छद्यत्र सो ऽनन्तो नागभोगपतिर् हरिः
शीघ्रं विक्रमतस्तस्य पद्भ्याम् आक्रान्तपीडिताः ॥
1.20.m: he came to where Hari was, that Ananta, the lord of serpent-coils. / As he strode swiftly, [the waters] trampled and pressed down by his two feet

1.20.s:
udbhūtāstūrṇamākāśe pṛthulāstoyabindavaḥ
atyuṣṇaścātiśītaś ca vāyustatra vavau punaḥ //
1.20.d:
उद्भूतास्तूर्णमाकाशे पृथुलास्तोयबिन्दवः
अत्युष्णश्चातिशीतश् च वायुस्तत्र ववौ पुनः ॥
1.20.m: produced large drops of water that quickly flew up into the air, / and an exceedingly hot and exceedingly cold wind blew there once again.

1.20.s:
taddṛṣṭvā mahadāścaryaṃ brahmā viṣṇumabhāṣata
abbindavaś ca śītoṣṇāḥ kampayantyaṃbujaṃ bhṛśam //
1.20.d:
तद्दृष्ट्वा महदाश्चर्यं ब्रह्मा विष्णुमभाषत
अब्बिन्दवश् च शीतोष्णाः कम्पयन्त्यंबुजं भृशम् ॥
1.20.m: Seeing that great wonder, Brahmā spoke to Viṣṇu: / “The drops of water, both cold and hot, are shaking the lotus violently.”

1.20.s:
etanme saṃśayaṃ brūhi kiṃ vā tvanyaccikīrṣasi
etadevaṃvidhaṃ vākyaṃ pitāmahamukhodgatam //
1.20.d:
एतन्मे संशयं ब्रूहि किं वा त्वन्यच्चिकीर्षसि
एतदेवंविधं वाक्यं पितामहमुखोद्गतम् ॥
1.20.m:
"Resolve this doubt of mine, or tell me what else you wish to do."
Having heard these words uttered from the mouth of Pitāmaha,

1.20.s:
śrutvāpratimakarmā hi bhagavānasurāntakṛt
kiṃ nu khalvatra me nābhyāṃ bhūtamanyatkṛtālayam //
1.20.d:
श्रुत्वाप्रतिमकर्मा हि भगवानसुरान्तकृत्
किं नु खल्वत्र मे नाभ्यां भूतमन्यत्कृतालयम् ॥
1.20.m:
the blessed destroyer of the asuras, whose deeds are matchless, [thought]:
"Can it be that some other creature has made its abode in my navel?

1.20.s:
vadati priyamatyarthaṃ manyuścāsya mayā kṛtaḥ
ityevaṃ manasā dhyātvā pratyuvācedamuttaram //
1.20.d:
वदति प्रियमत्यर्थं मन्युश्चास्य मया कृतः
इत्येवं मनसा ध्यात्वा प्रत्युवाचेदमुत्तरम् ॥
1.20.m:
He speaks so very affectionately, yet I caused him anger."
Having pondered this in his mind, he spoke this answer:

1.20.s:
kimatra bhagavānadya puṣkare jātasaṃbhramaḥ
kiṃ mayā ca kṛtaṃ deva yanmāṃ priyamanuttamam //
1.20.d:
किमत्र भगवानद्य पुष्करे जातसंभ्रमः
किं मया च कृतं देव यन्मां प्रियमनुत्तमम् ॥
1.20.m:
"Why is the Blessed One agitated today upon the lotus?
And what have I done, O god, that you speak to me so exceedingly

1.20.s:
bhāṣase puruṣaśreṣṭha kimarthaṃ brūhi tattvataḥ
evaṃ bruvāṇaṃ deveśaṃ lokayātrānugaṃ tataḥ //
1.20.d:
भाषसे पुरुषश्रेष्ठ किमर्थं ब्रूहि तत्त्वतः
एवं ब्रुवाणं देवेशं लोकयात्रानुगं ततः ॥
1.20.m:
kindly, O best of men? Tell me truly what the reason is."
To the lord of the gods speaking thus, conforming to worldly conduct,

1.20.s:
pratyuvācāmbujābhākṣaṃ brahmā vedanidhiḥ prabhuḥ
yo 'sau tavodaraṃ pūrvaṃ praviṣṭo 'haṃ tvadicchayā //
1.20.d:
प्रत्युवाचाम्बुजाभाक्षं ब्रह्मा वेदनिधिः प्रभुः
यो ऽसौ तवोदरं पूर्वं प्रविष्टो ऽहं त्वदिच्छया ॥
1.20.m:
Brahmā, the treasury of the Vedas and the lord, replied to the lotus-eyed one:
"When formerly I entered your belly of your own accord,

1.20.s:
yathā mamodare lokāḥ sarve dṛṣṭāstvayā prabho
tathaiva dṛṣṭāḥ kārtsnyena mayā lokāstavodare //
1.20.d:
यथा ममोदरे लोकाः सर्वे दृष्टास्त्वया प्रभो
तथैव दृष्टाः कार्त्स्न्येन मया लोकास्तवोदरे ॥
1.20.m:
just as all the worlds were seen by you in my belly, O lord,
even so were all the worlds seen entirely by me in your belly.

1.20.s:
tato varṣasahasrāttu upāvṛttasya me 'nagha
tvayā matsarabhāvena māṃ vaśīkartumicchatā //
1.20.d:
ततो वर्षसहस्रात्तु उपावृत्तस्य मे ऽनघ
त्वया मत्सरभावेन मां वशीकर्तुमिच्छता ॥
1.20.m:
Then, after a thousand years had passed, as I was returning, O sinless one,
you, out of envy and desiring to subjugate me,

1.20.s:
āśu dvārāṇi sarvāṇi pihitāni samantataḥ
tato mayā mahābhāga saṃcintya svena tejasā //
1.20.d:
आशु द्वाराणि सर्वाणि पिहितानि समन्ततः
ततो मया महाभाग संचिन्त्य स्वेन तेजसा ॥
1.20.m:
quickly shut all the doors on every side.
Then by me, O illustrious one, having reflected by my own splendor,

1.20.s:
labdho nābhipradeśena padmasūtrādvinirgamaḥ
mā bhūtte manaso 'lpo 'pi vyāghāto 'yaṃ kathaṃcana //
1.20.d:
लब्धो नाभिप्रदेशेन पद्मसूत्राद्विनिर्गमः
मा भूत्ते मनसो ऽल्पो ऽपि व्याघातो ऽयं कथंचन ॥
1.20.m:
an exit was found by way of the navel through the stalk of the lotus.
Let there be not the slightest distress in your mind in any way.

1.20.s:
ityeṣānugatirviṣṇo kāryāṇām aupasarpiṇī
yanmayānantaraṃ kāryaṃ brūhi kiṃ karavāṇyaham //
1.20.d:
इत्येषानुगतिर्विष्णो कार्याणाम् औपसर्पिणी
यन्मयानन्तरं कार्यं ब्रूहि किं करवाण्यहम् ॥
1.20.m:
Such is the sequential course of deeds, O Viṣṇu.
Tell me what I must do next, what work I should perform."

1.20.s:
tataḥ paramameyātmā hiraṇyakaśipo ripuḥ
anavadyāṃ priyāmiṣṭāṃ śivāṃ vāṇīṃ pitāmahāt //
1.20.d:
ततः परममेयात्मा हिरण्यकशिपो रिपुः
अनवद्यां प्रियामिष्टां शिवां वाणीं पितामहात् ॥
1.20.m:
Then the enemy of Hiraṇyakaśipu, possessed of an infinitely immeasurable self,
having heard from Pitāmaha those faultless, affectionate, dear, and auspicious words,

1.20.s:
śrutvā vigatamātsaryaṃ vākyamasmai dadau hariḥ
na hyevamīdṛśaṃ kāryaṃ mayādhyavasitaṃ tava //
1.20.d:
श्रुत्वा विगतमात्सर्यं वाक्यमस्मै ददौ हरिः
न ह्येवमीदृशं कार्यं मयाध्यवसितं तव ॥
1.20.m:
Hari, freed from envy, replied to him with this speech:
"Indeed, no such hostile act against you was intended by me.

1.20.s:
tvāṃ bodhayitukāmena krīḍāpūrvaṃ yadṛcchayā
āśu dvārāṇi sarvāṇi ghāṭitāni mayātmanaḥ //
1.20.d:
त्वां बोधयितुकामेन क्रीडापूर्वं यदृच्छया
आशु द्वाराणि सर्वाणि घाटितानि मयात्मनः ॥
1.20.m:
Desiring to instruct you, in spontaneous sport,
all the doors of my own self were quickly closed by me.

1.20.s:
na te 'nyathāvagantavyaṃ mānyaḥ pūjyaś ca me bhavān
sarvaṃ marṣaya kalyāṇa yanmayāpakṛtaṃ tava //
1.20.d:
न ते ऽन्यथावगन्तव्यं मान्यः पूज्यश् च मे भवान्
सर्वं मर्षय कल्याण यन्मयापकृतं तव ॥
1.20.m:
You must not understand it otherwise; you are respected and worthy of my worship.
Forgive everything, O blessed one, whatever wrong I have done to you.

1.20.s:
asmān mayohyamānastvaṃ padmādavatara prabho
nāhaṃ bhavantaṃ śaknomi soḍhuṃ tejomayaṃ gurum //
1.20.d:
अस्मान् मयोह्यमानस्त्वं पद्मादवतर प्रभो
नाहं भवन्तं शक्नोमि सोढुं तेजोमयं गुरुम् ॥
1.20.m:
Descend, O lord, from this lotus that is carried by me.
I am not able to bear you, heavy and full of splendor."

1.20.s:
sa hovāca varaṃ brūhi padmādavatara prabho
putro bhava mamārighna mudaṃ prāpsyasi śobhanām //
1.20.d:
स होवाच वरं ब्रूहि पद्मादवतर प्रभो
पुत्रो भव ममारिघ्न मुदं प्राप्स्यसि शोभनाम् ॥
1.20.m:
He indeed said: "Choose a boon, descend from the lotus, O lord.
Become my son, O slayer of foes, and you will attain radiant joy.

1.20.s:
sadbhāvavacanaṃ brūhi padmādavatara prabho
sa tvaṃ ca no mahāyogī tvamīḍyaḥ praṇavātmakaḥ //
1.20.d:
सद्भाववचनं ब्रूहि पद्मादवतर प्रभो
स त्वं च नो महायोगी त्वमीड्यः प्रणवात्मकः ॥
1.20.m:
Speak a word of true benevolence; descend from the lotus, O lord.
For you are our great yogin, you are praiseworthy, having the nature of the praṇava.

1.20.s:
adyaprabhṛti sarveśaḥ śvetoṣṇīṣavibhūṣitaḥ
padmayoniriti hyevaṃ khyāto nāmnā bhaviṣyasi //
1.20.d:
अद्यप्रभृति सर्वेशः श्वेतोष्णीषविभूषितः
पद्मयोनिरिति ह्येवं ख्यातो नाम्ना भविष्यसि ॥
1.20.m:
From this day forth, you, the ruler of all, adorned with a white turban,
will become famous indeed by the name Padmayoni ('Lotus-born').

1.20.s:
putro me tvaṃ bhava brahman saptalokādhipaḥ prabho
tataḥ sa bhagavāndevo varaṃ dattvā kirīṭine //
1.20.d:
पुत्रो मे त्वं भव ब्रह्मन् सप्तलोकाधिपः प्रभो
ततः स भगवान्देवो वरं दत्त्वा किरीटिने ॥
1.20.m:
Become my son, O Brahman, the lord and master of the seven worlds."
Then that blessed god, having granted the boon to the diadem-wearer,

1.20.s:
evaṃ bhavatu cetyuktvā prītātmā gatamatsaraḥ
pratyāsannam athāyāntaṃ bālārkābhaṃ mahānanam //
1.20.d:
एवं भवतु चेत्युक्त्वा प्रीतात्मा गतमत्सरः
प्रत्यासन्नम् अथायान्तं बालार्काभं महाननम् ॥
1.20.m:
saying 'So be it,' pleased in self and rid of jealousy,
beheld approaching nearby Bhava, shining like the morning sun, with a huge face,

1.20.s:
bhavamatyadbhutaṃ dṛṣṭvā nārāyaṇamathābravīt
aprameyo mahāvaktro daṃṣṭrī dhvastaśiroruhaḥ //
1.20.d:
भवमत्यद्भुतं दृष्ट्वा नारायणमथाब्रवीत्
अप्रमेयो महावक्त्रो दंष्ट्री ध्वस्तशिरोरुहः ॥
1.20.m:
exceedingly wonderful, and he then spoke to Nārāyaṇa:
"[He is] immeasurable, large-faced, fanged, with disheveled hair,

1.20.s:
daśabāhustriśūlāṅko nayanairviśvataḥ sthitaḥ
lokaprabhuḥ svayaṃ sākṣād vikṛto muñjamekhalī //
1.20.d:
दशबाहुस्त्रिशूलाङ्को नयनैर्विश्वतः स्थितः
लोकप्रभुः स्वयं साक्षाद् विकृतो मुञ्जमेखली ॥
1.20.m:
ten-armed, marked by the trident, standing with eyes on every side,
himself the lord of the world manifest, deformed, wearing a belt of muñja grass,

1.20.s:
meṇḍhreṇordhvena mahatā nardamāno 'tibhairavam
kaḥ khalveṣa pumān viṣṇo tejorāśir mahādyutiḥ //
1.20.d:
मेण्ढ्रेणोर्ध्वेन महता नर्दमानो ऽतिभैरवम्
कः खल्वेष पुमान् विष्णो तेजोराशिर् महाद्युतिः ॥
1.20.m:
with an erect, huge phallus, roaring most dreadfully!
Who indeed is this man, O Viṣṇu, a mass of splendor and great radiance,

1.20.s:
vyāpya sarvā diśo dyāṃ ca ita evābhivartate
tenaivamukto bhagavān viṣṇurbrahmāṇamabravīt //
1.20.d:
व्याप्य सर्वा दिशो द्यां च इत एवाभिवर्तते
तेनैवमुक्तो भगवान् विष्णुर्ब्रह्माणमब्रवीत् ॥
1.20.m:
who, pervading all directions and heaven, advances right here?"
Addressed thus by him, the blessed Viṣṇu said to Brahmā:

1.20.s:
padbhyāṃ talanipātena yasya vikramato 'rṇave
vegena mahatākāśe 'pyutthitāś ca jalaśayāḥ //
1.20.d:
पद्भ्यां तलनिपातेन यस्य विक्रमतो ऽर्णवे
वेगेन महताकाशे ऽप्युत्थिताश् च जलशयाः ॥
1.20.m:
"By the tread of whose feet stamping down as he strides in the ocean
reservoirs of water have risen up with great force even into the sky,

1.20.s:
sthūlādbhir viśvato 'tyarthaṃ sicyase padmasaṃbhava
ghrāṇajena ca vātena kampyamānaṃ tvayā saha //
1.20.d:
स्थूलाद्भिर् विश्वतो ऽत्यर्थं सिच्यसे पद्मसंभव
घ्राणजेन च वातेन कम्प्यमानं त्वया सह ॥
1.20.m:
by which large drops of water you are profusely sprinkled all over, O lotus-born one,
and by the wind arising from his nostrils, shaken along with you,

1.20.s:
dodhūyate mahāpadmaṃ svacchandaṃ mama nābhijam
samāgato bhavānīśo hy anādiścāntakṛtprabhuḥ //
1.20.d:
दोधूयते महापद्मं स्वच्छन्दं मम नाभिजम्
समागतो भवानीशो ह्य् अनादिश्चान्तकृत्प्रभुः ॥
1.20.m:
this great lotus born from my navel is tossing violently at will.
Bhava the Lord has arrived, the beginningless and destroying master.

1.20.s:
bhavānahaṃ ca stotreṇa upatiṣṭhāva godhvajam
tataḥ kruddho 'mbujābhākṣaṃ brahmā provāca keśavam //
1.20.d:
भवानहं च स्तोत्रेण उपतिष्ठाव गोध्वजम्
ततः क्रुद्धो ऽम्बुजाभाक्षं ब्रह्मा प्रोवाच केशवम् ॥
1.20.m:
Let you and me wait upon the bull-bannered god with a hymn of praise."
Then Brahmā, angered, said to Keśava, whose eyes are like lotuses:

1.20.s:
bhavānna nūnamātmānaṃ vetti lokaprabhuṃ vibhum
brahmāṇaṃ lokakartāraṃ māṃ na vetsi sanātanam //
1.20.d:
भवान्न नूनमात्मानं वेत्ति लोकप्रभुं विभुम्
ब्रह्माणं लोककर्तारं मां न वेत्सि सनातनम् ॥
1.20.m:
"Surely you do not know yourself to be the all-pervading lord of the world,
nor do you know me, Brahmā, the eternal creator of the worlds!

1.20.s:
ko hyasau śaṅkaro nāma āvayorvyatiricyate
tasya tatkrodhajaṃ vākyaṃ śrutvā harirabhāṣata //
1.20.d:
को ह्यसौ शङ्करो नाम आवयोर्व्यतिरिच्यते
तस्य तत्क्रोधजं वाक्यं श्रुत्वा हरिरभाषत ॥
1.20.m:
Who indeed is this one called Śaṅkara that he should be superior to the two of us?"
Having heard that speech of his born of anger, Hari spoke:

1.20.s:
mā maivaṃ vada kalyāṇa parivādaṃ mahātmanaḥ
mahāyogendhano dharmo durādharṣo varapradaḥ //
1.20.d:
मा मैवं वद कल्याण परिवादं महात्मनः
महायोगेन्धनो धर्मो दुराधर्षो वरप्रदः ॥
1.20.m:
"Do not say so, O blessed one! Speak no slander of the Great Self!
He is dharma, the kindling for the great yoga, unassailable, the granter of boons,

1.20.s:
heturasyātha jagataḥ purāṇapuruṣo 'vyayaḥ
bījī khalveṣa bījānāṃ jyotirekaḥ prakāśate //
1.20.d:
हेतुरस्याथ जगतः पुराणपुरुषो ऽव्ययः
बीजी खल्वेष बीजानां ज्योतिरेकः प्रकाशते ॥
1.20.m:
the cause of this universe, the ancient and imperishable Puruṣa.
He is the sower of the seeds, the single light that shines.

1.20.s:
bālakrīḍanakairdevaḥ krīḍate śaṅkaraḥ svayam
pradhānamavyayo yonir avyaktaṃ prakṛtistamaḥ //
1.20.d:
बालक्रीडनकैर्देवः क्रीडते शङ्करः स्वयम्
प्रधानमव्ययो योनिर् अव्यक्तं प्रकृतिस्तमः ॥
1.20.m:
The god Śaṅkara plays by himself as though with children's toys.
Pradhāna, the imperishable womb, the unmanifest, prakṛti, and tamas —

1.20.s:
mama caitāni nāmāni nityaṃ prasavadharmiṇaḥ
yaḥ kaḥ sa iti duḥkhārtair dṛśyate yatibhiḥ śivaḥ //
1.20.d:
मम चैतानि नामानि नित्यं प्रसवधर्मिणः
यः कः स इति दुःखार्तैर् दृश्यते यतिभिः शिवः ॥
1.20.m:
these are my names, since I have the eternal attribute of bringing forth.
Śiva is seen by ascetics distressed by sorrow, [wondering] 'Who or what is he?'

1.20.s:
eṣa bījī bhavānbījam ahaṃ yoniḥ sanātanaḥ
sa evamukto viśvātmā brahmā viṣṇumapṛcchata //
1.20.d:
एष बीजी भवान्बीजम् अहं योनिः सनातनः
स एवमुक्तो विश्वात्मा ब्रह्मा विष्णुमपृच्छत ॥
1.20.m:
He is the sower, you are the seed, and I am the eternal womb."
Addressed thus, Brahmā, the self of the universe, inquired of Viṣṇu:

1.20.s:
bhavān yonirahaṃ bījaṃ kathaṃ bījī maheśvaraḥ
etanme sūkṣmamavyaktaṃ saṃśayaṃ chettumarhasi //
1.20.d:
भवान् योनिरहं बीजं कथं बीजी महेश्वरः
एतन्मे सूक्ष्ममव्यक्तं संशयं छेत्तुमर्हसि ॥
1.20.m:
"You are the womb, I am the seed, but how is Maheśvara the sower?
You ought to sever this subtle and unmanifest doubt of mine."

1.20.s:
jñātvā ca vividhotpattiṃ brahmaṇo lokatantriṇaḥ
imaṃ paramasādṛśyaṃ praśnam abhyavadaddhariḥ //
1.20.d:
ज्ञात्वा च विविधोत्पत्तिं ब्रह्मणो लोकतन्त्रिणः
इमं परमसादृश्यं प्रश्नम् अभ्यवदद्धरिः ॥
1.20.m:
And knowing the diverse origin of Brahmā, the director of the world,
Hari answered this question concerning supreme similarity:

1.20.s:
asmānmahattaraṃ bhūtaṃ guhyamanyanna vidyate
mahataḥ paramaṃ dhāma śivam adhyātmināṃ padam //
1.20.d:
अस्मान्महत्तरं भूतं गुह्यमन्यन्न विद्यते
महतः परमं धाम शिवम् अध्यात्मिनां पदम् ॥
1.20.m:
"No other secret being greater than this exists;
[he is] the supreme abode of the Great One, Śiva, the goal of those devoted to the inner self.

1.20.s:
dvividhaṃ caivamātmānaṃ pravibhajya vyavasthitaḥ
niṣkalastatra yo 'vyaktaḥ sakalaś ca maheśvaraḥ //
1.20.d:
द्विविधं चैवमात्मानं प्रविभज्य व्यवस्थितः
निष्कलस्तत्र यो ऽव्यक्तः सकलश् च महेश्वरः ॥
1.20.m:
Having thus divided his self into two forms, he remains established:
therein Maheśvara is both without parts (unmanifest) and with parts.

1.20.s:
yasya māyāvidhijñasya agamyagahanasya ca
purā liṅgodbhavaṃ bījaṃ prathamaṃ tvādisargikam //
1.20.d:
यस्य मायाविधिज्ञस्य अगम्यगहनस्य च
पुरा लिङ्गोद्भवं बीजं प्रथमं त्वादिसर्गिकम् ॥
1.20.m:
Of him who knows the rules of māyā and is unapproachable and unfathomable,
the primary seed born of the liṅga formerly at the primordial creation

1.20.s:
mama yonau samāyuktaṃ tadbījaṃ kālaparyayāt
hiraṇmayamakūpāre yonyāmaṇḍamajāyata //
1.20.d:
मम योनौ समायुक्तं तद्बीजं कालपर्ययात्
हिरण्मयमकूपारे योन्यामण्डमजायत ॥
1.20.m:
was united in my womb; by the passage of time that seed
became a golden egg in the womb within the ocean.

1.20.s:
śatāni daśa varṣāṇām aṇḍam apsu pratiṣṭhitam
ante varṣasahasrasya vāyunā taddvidhā kṛtam //
1.20.d:
शतानि दश वर्षाणाम् अण्डम् अप्सु प्रतिष्ठितम्
अन्ते वर्षसहस्रस्य वायुना तद्द्विधा कृतम् ॥
1.20.m:
For ten hundred years the egg rested in the waters;
at the end of a thousand years, it was split in two by the wind.

1.20.s:
kapālamekaṃ dyaurjajñe kapālamaparaṃ kṣitiḥ
ulbaṃ tasya mahotsedho yo 'sau kanakaparvataḥ //
1.20.d:
कपालमेकं द्यौर्जज्ञे कपालमपरं क्षितिः
उल्बं तस्य महोत्सेधो यो ऽसौ कनकपर्वतः ॥
1.20.m:
One shell became the sky, and the other shell became the earth;
its outer skin is that great elevation which is the golden mountain [Meru].

1.20.s:
tataś ca pratisaṃdhyātmā devadevo varaḥ prabhuḥ
hiraṇyagarbho bhagavāṃs tv abhijajñe caturmukhaḥ //
1.20.d:
ततश् च प्रतिसंध्यात्मा देवदेवो वरः प्रभुः
हिरण्यगर्भो भगवांस् त्व् अभिजज्ञे चतुर्मुखः ॥
1.20.m:
And then, having the nature of each dawn twilight, the supreme god of gods, the lord,
the blessed Hiraṇyagarbha, the four-faced one, was born.

1.20.s:
ā tārārkendunakṣatraṃ śūnyaṃ lokamavekṣya ca
ko 'hamityapi ca dhyāte kumārāste 'bhavaṃstadā //
1.20.d:
आ तारार्केन्दुनक्षत्रं शून्यं लोकमवेक्ष्य च
को ऽहमित्यपि च ध्याते कुमारास्ते ऽभवंस्तदा ॥
1.20.m:
And beholding the world empty up to the stars, sun, moon, and asterisms,
when he meditated, thinking 'Who am I?', your Kumāras then came into being,

1.20.s:
priyadarśanāstu yatayo yatīnāṃ pūrvajās tava
bhūyo varṣasahasrānte tata evātmajāstava //
1.20.d:
प्रियदर्शनास्तु यतयो यतीनां पूर्वजास् तव
भूयो वर्षसहस्रान्ते तत एवात्मजास्तव ॥
1.20.m:
fair to behold, ascetics, the elders among your ascetics.
Then, at the end of another thousand years, from him your sons were born.

1.20.s:
bhuvanānalasaṃkāśāḥ padmapatrāyatekṣaṇāḥ
śrīmānsanatkumāraś ca ṛbhuścaivordhvaretasau //
1.20.d:
भुवनानलसंकाशाः पद्मपत्रायतेक्षणाः
श्रीमान्सनत्कुमारश् च ऋभुश्चैवोर्ध्वरेतसौ ॥
1.20.m: Resembling cosmic fire, with eyes long as lotus petals, / the glorious Sanatkumāra and Ṛbhu, both possessing drawn-up seed,

1.20.s:
sanakaḥ sanātanaścaiva tathaiva ca sanandanaḥ
utpannāḥ samakālaṃ te buddhyātīndriyadarśanāḥ //
1.20.d:
सनकः सनातनश्चैव तथैव च सनन्दनः
उत्पन्नाः समकालं ते बुद्ध्यातीन्द्रियदर्शनाः ॥
