kimatra devadevasya mūrtyaṣṭakamidaṃ jagat //
1.28.d:
कर्मणा तस्य चैवेह जगत्सर्वं प्रतिष्ठितम्
किमत्र देवदेवस्य मूर्त्यष्टकमिदं जगत् ॥
1.28.m: And by his action the entire world is established here. / What [need to say] here of the God of gods? This world is his eightfold form:

1.28.s:
vinākāśaṃ jagannaiva vinā kṣmāṃ vāyunā vinā
tejasā vāriṇā caiva yajamānaṃ tathā vinā //
1.28.d:
विनाकाशं जगन्नैव विना क्ष्मां वायुना विना
तेजसा वारिणा चैव यजमानं तथा विना ॥
1.28.m: the world does not exist without space, nor without earth, nor without wind, / nor without fire and water, nor likewise without the sacrificer,

1.28.s:
bhānunā śaśinā lokas tasyaitāstanavaḥ prabhoḥ
vicāratastu rudrasya sthūlametaccarācaram //
1.28.d:
भानुना शशिना लोकस् तस्यैतास्तनवः प्रभोः
विचारतस्तु रुद्रस्य स्थूलमेतच्चराचरम् ॥
1.28.m: nor without the sun and moon: these are the bodies of that Lord. / Upon inquiry, this moving and unmoving world is the gross [body] of Rudra;

1.28.s:
sūkṣmaṃ vadanti ṛṣayo yanna vācyaṃ dvijottamāḥ
yato vāco nivartante aprāpya manasā saha //
1.28.d:
सूक्ष्मं वदन्ति ऋषयो यन्न वाच्यं द्विजोत्तमाः
यतो वाचो निवर्तन्ते अप्राप्य मनसा सह ॥
1.28.m: the sages speak of the subtle, which cannot be expressed in words, O best of the twice-born, / 'from which words turn back, along with the mind, without having reached it.'

1.28.s:
ānandaṃ brahmaṇo vidvān na bibheti kutaścana
na bhetavyaṃ tathā tasmāj jñātvānandaṃ pinākinaḥ //
1.28.d:
आनन्दं ब्रह्मणो विद्वान् न बिभेति कुतश्चन
न भेतव्यं तथा तस्माज् ज्ञात्वानन्दं पिनाकिनः ॥
1.28.m: 'Knowing the bliss of Brahman, he fears nothing from anywhere;' / likewise, knowing the bliss of Pinākin, one should not fear from that [world].

1.28.s:
vibhūtayaś ca rudrasya matvā sarvatra bhāvataḥ
sarvaṃ rudra iti prāhur munayastattvadarśinaḥ //
1.28.d:
विभूतयश् च रुद्रस्य मत्वा सर्वत्र भावतः
सर्वं रुद्र इति प्राहुर् मुनयस्तत्त्वदर्शिनः ॥
1.28.m: Having recognized the manifestations of Rudra everywhere with devotion, / the sages who perceive the truth declared that everything is Rudra.

1.28.s:
namaskāreṇa satataṃ gauravātparameṣṭhinaḥ
sarvaṃ tu khalvidaṃ brahma sarvo vai rudra īśvaraḥ //
1.28.d:
नमस्कारेण सततं गौरवात्परमेष्ठिनः
सर्वं तु खल्विदं ब्रह्म सर्वो वै रुद्र ईश्वरः ॥
1.28.m: With constant bow out of reverence for Parameṣṭhin, / 'all this indeed is Brahman; all is Rudra, the Lord.'

1.28.s:
puruṣo vai mahādevo maheśānaḥ paraḥ śivaḥ
evaṃ vibhurvinirdiṣṭo dhyānaṃ tatraiva cintanam //
1.28.d:
पुरुषो वै महादेवो महेशानः परः शिवः
एवं विभुर्विनिर्दिष्टो ध्यानं तत्रैव चिन्तनम् ॥
1.28.m: Puruṣa is indeed Mahādeva, Maheśāna, the supreme Śiva; / thus the all-pervading Lord is designated; meditation is contemplation upon him alone.

1.28.s:
caturvyūheṇa mārgeṇa vicāryālokya suvrata
saṃsārahetuḥ saṃsāro mokṣahetuś ca nirvṛtiḥ //
1.28.d:
चतुर्व्यूहेण मार्गेण विचार्यालोक्य सुव्रत
संसारहेतुः संसारो मोक्षहेतुश् च निर्वृतिः ॥
1.28.m: Having reflected and observed by the fourfold method, O you of good vows: / the cause of saṃsāra, saṃsāra [itself], the cause of liberation, and liberation,

1.28.s:
caturvyūhaḥ samākhyātaś cintakasyeha yoginaḥ
cintā bahuvidhā khyātā saikatra parameṣṭhinā //
1.28.d:
चतुर्व्यूहः समाख्यातश् चिन्तकस्येह योगिनः
चिन्ता बहुविधा ख्याता सैकत्र परमेष्ठिना ॥
1.28.m: the fourfold scheme has been fully described here for the yogin who contemplates. / Contemplation is taught to be manifold; focused on the one Parameṣṭhin,

1.28.s:
suniṣṭhetyatra kathitā rudraṃ raudrī na saṃśayaḥ
aindrī cendre tathā saumyā some nārāyaṇe tathā //
1.28.d:
सुनिष्ठेत्यत्र कथिता रुद्रं रौद्री न संशयः
ऐन्द्री चेन्द्रे तथा सौम्या सोमे नारायणे तथा ॥
1.28.m: it is called steadfast here, directed towards Rudra, of the nature of Rudra, without doubt; / relating to Indra in Indra, relating to Soma in Soma, and likewise in Nārāyaṇa,

1.28.s:
sūrye vahnau ca sarveṣāṃ sarvatraivaṃ vicārataḥ
saivāhaṃ so 'hamityevaṃ dvidhā saṃsthāpya bhāvataḥ //
1.28.d:
सूर्ये वह्नौ च सर्वेषां सर्वत्रैवं विचारतः
सैवाहं सो ऽहमित्येवं द्विधा संस्थाप्य भावतः ॥
1.28.m: in the sun, and in fire, for all beings, upon inquiry everywhere in this way. / Having established [it] through devotion in two ways, as 'I am that [energy]' and 'I am he',

1.28.s:
bhakto 'sau nāsti yastasmāc cintā brāhmī na saṃśayaḥ
evaṃ brahmamayaṃ dhyāyet pūrvaṃ vipra carācaram //
1.28.d:
भक्तो ऽसौ नास्ति यस्तस्माच् चिन्ता ब्राह्मी न संशयः
एवं ब्रह्ममयं ध्यायेत् पूर्वं विप्र चराचरम् ॥
1.28.m: since that devotee does not exist [apart from him], contemplation is of the nature of Brahman, without doubt. / Thus one should first meditate on the moving and unmoving world as consisting of Brahman, O brāhmaṇa;

1.28.s:
carācaravibhāgaṃ ca tyajedabhimataṃ smaran
tyājyaṃ grāhyam alabhyaṃ ca kṛtyaṃ cākṛtyameva ca //
1.28.d:
चराचरविभागं च त्यजेदभिमतं स्मरन्
त्याज्यं ग्राह्यम् अलभ्यं च कृत्यं चाकृत्यमेव च ॥
1.28.m: and remembering what is desired, he should abandon the distinction of the moving and unmoving, / what is to be abandoned, what is to be grasped, what is unattainable, what is to be done, and what is not to be done.

1.28.s:
yasya nāsti sutṛptasya tasya brāhmī na cānyathā
ābhyantaraṃ samākhyātam evamabhyarcanaṃ kramāt //
1.28.d:
यस्य नास्ति सुतृप्तस्य तस्य ब्राह्मी न चान्यथा
आभ्यन्तरं समाख्यातम् एवमभ्यर्चनं क्रमात् ॥
1.28.m: For him who is completely content, who has nothing [to discard or take], meditation on Brahman occurs, and not otherwise. / Thus inner worship has been expounded in due order.

1.28.s:
ābhyantarārcakāḥ pūjyā namaskārādibhis tathā
virūpā vikṛtāścāpi na nindyā brahmavādinaḥ //
1.28.d:
आभ्यन्तरार्चकाः पूज्या नमस्कारादिभिस् तथा
विरूपा विकृताश्चापि न निन्द्या ब्रह्मवादिनः ॥
1.28.m: Those who perform inner worship are to be honoured with salutations and the like; / even if misshapen and deformed, those who speak of Brahman must not be reviled.

1.28.s:
ābhyantarārcakāḥ sarve na parīkṣyā vijānatā
nindakā eva duḥkhārtā bhaviṣyantyalpacetasaḥ //
1.28.d:
आभ्यन्तरार्चकाः सर्वे न परीक्ष्या विजानता
निन्दका एव दुःखार्ता भविष्यन्त्यल्पचेतसः ॥
1.28.m: None of the inner worshippers should be tested by one who knows; / revilers will only become afflicted with sorrow, small-minded as they are.

1.28.s:
yathā dāruvane rudraṃ vinindya munayaḥ purā
tasmātsevyā namaskāryāḥ sadā brahmavidas tathā //
1.28.d:
यथा दारुवने रुद्रं विनिन्द्य मुनयः पुरा
तस्मात्सेव्या नमस्कार्याः सदा ब्रह्मविदस् तथा ॥
1.28.m: Just as the sages of old, having reviled Rudra in the pine forest, [suffered]; / therefore those who know Brahman should always be served and saluted

1.28.s: varṇāśramavinirmuktā varṇāśramaparāyaṇaiḥ //
1.28.d: वर्णाश्रमविनिर्मुक्ता वर्णाश्रमपरायणैः ॥
1.28.m: by those devoted to caste and stage of life, though [the former] are free from caste and stage of life.
